sec02-card-sec02-F031.teaching_text: Repeated safety disregard, hazardous privilege misuse, or involvement in a fatal or serious-injury crash puts young licenses at risk.

sec02-card-sec02-F032.question_text: What alcohol-concentration percentages define legal intoxication generally versus for drivers under twenty-one?
sec02-card-sec02-F032.teaching_text: Underage drivers hit the per-se alcohol standard at one-fourth of the adult threshold, leaving zero margin for drinking.

sec02-card-sec02-F033.question_text: Which chemical tests do you consent to by driving in New Hampshire after an impairment arrest, and what if you refuse?
sec02-card-sec02-F033.teaching_text: Refusing post-arrest blood, breath, urine, or combined testing triggers administrative loss of driving privileges on its own.

sec02-card-sec02-F034.question_text: What can piling up excessive demerit points cause, and what driver factor changes the threshold?
sec02-card-sec02-F034.teaching_text: Younger drivers hit suspension thresholds at lower point totals than older motorists, so age governs how fast points bite.

sec02-card-sec02-F035.question_text: Which common moving violations does the manual name as examples that add demerit points?
sec02-card-sec02-F035.teaching_text: Everyday tickets like speeding, blowing stop signs or signals, improper passing, and impaired driving stack demerit points quickly.

sec02-card-sec02-F036.question_text: How can a traffic offense committed outside New Hampshire affect your home record?
sec02-card-sec02-F036.teaching_text: Crossing state borders offers zero shield because outside convictions get reported back and impact your New Hampshire privileges.

sec02-card-sec02-F037.question_text: Following a required hearing, how long can a habitual-offender revocation last?
sec02-card-sec02-F037.teaching_text: Accumulating serious or repeated convictions triggers a formal hearing and strips driving rights for one to four years.

sec02-card-sec02-F038.question_text: What prison sentence range can follow driving after being declared a habitual offender?
sec02-card-sec02-F038.teaching_text: Getting caught behind the wheel under habitual-offender revocation carries severe felony-scale imprisonment from one to five years.

sec07-card-sec07-F001.question_text: Which two payment methods does the New Hampshire handbook describe for turnpike tolls?
sec07-card-sec07-F001.teaching_text: Spotting purple EZPass overhead banners versus cash-booth signs early keeps you out of wrong-lane scrambles.

sec07-card-sec07-F002.question_text: What speed, stopping, and cabin rules apply inside a staffed cash toll lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F002.teaching_text: Stepping out onto greasy plaza concrete for dropped coins exposes you to rolling cars in tight lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F003.question_text: What two maneuvers are strictly forbidden if you enter the wrong lane at a toll plaza?
sec07-card-sec07-F003.teaching_text: Reversing out of a toll chute sends you straight into fast-approaching turnpike traffic behind you.

sec07-card-sec07-F004.question_text: How must you drive through an electronic EZPass lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F004.teaching_text: Braking to a stop under an electronic toll gantry invites an immediate rear-end collision.

sec07-card-sec07-F005.question_text: What must you check on each corner and switch on before starting any turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F005.teaching_text: Checking every corner catches cyclists, joggers, and no-turn signs before your wheels commit.

sec07-card-sec07-F006.question_text: Where within your lane should you position the car before turning, and where should your eyes look?
sec07-card-sec07-F006.teaching_text: Looking deep down your target street guides smooth steering and spots pedestrians or parked cars early.

sec07-card-sec07-F007.question_text: What three steps wrap up a turn cleanly once your car straightens out?
sec07-card-sec07-F007.teaching_text: Leaving a turn signal blinking confuses cross-street drivers into pulling out right in front of you.

sec07-card-sec07-F008.question_text: From where in your lane does a right turn begin, and what wide steering habit must you avoid?
sec07-card-sec07-F008.teaching_text: Swinging wide left before turning right tricks trailing drivers into thinking you are changing lanes left.

sec07-card-sec07-F009.question_text: Where in your lane do you start a left turn, and to whom must you yield?
sec07-card-sec07-F009.teaching_text: Tucking against the left side of your lane lets straight-through traffic pass on your right where room allows.

sec07-card-sec07-F010.question_text: How must you handle lane choice and tracking where two or more lanes turn side by side?
sec07-card-sec07-F010.teaching_text: Drifting wide mid-intersection clips the car turning right alongside you in the outer arc.

sec07-card-sec07-F011.question_text: What is the only safe move after passing your exit on a divided highway?
sec07-card-sec07-F011.teaching_text: Stopping, reversing up a shoulder, or cutting across a median invites fatal high-speed freeway impacts.

sec07-card-sec07-F012.question_text: What must you verify before attempting a U-turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F012.teaching_text: Busy downtown blocks, blind hillcrests, curves, and signalized intersections frequently post strict no-U-turn restrictions.

sec07-card-sec07-F013.question_text: How does the New Hampshire handbook's U-turn procedure begin and finish?
sec07-card-sec07-F013.teaching_text: Starting from the right shoulder buys turning radius so you swing cleanly into the nearest opposing lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F014.question_text: When and using what roadside features do you perform a two-point turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F014.teaching_text: Using a driveway or alley reverses direction cleanly when circling the block is impossible.

sec07-card-sec07-F015.question_text: Why and how do you start a reverse two-point turn using a driveway on your right?
sec07-card-sec07-F015.teaching_text: Backing into the driveway while traffic is clear lets you pull forward into traffic with full front visibility.

sec07-card-sec07-F016.question_text: Once backed into the driveway during a reverse two-point turn, how do you re-enter the road?
sec07-card-sec07-F016.teaching_text: Pulling out nose-first gives clear sightlines both ways before turning left into your new lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F017.question_text: How do you enter a left-side driveway to begin a forward two-point turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F017.teaching_text: Pulling completely past the road edge near the driveway's right side clears live traffic before reversing.

sec07-card-sec07-F018.question_text: How do you back out and resume driving during the second half of a forward two-point turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F018.teaching_text: Backing into a live roadway is riskier than backing in, demanding full checks and a complete stop before shifting forward.

sec07-card-sec07-F019.question_text: On what specific type of road is a three-point turn appropriate?
sec07-card-sec07-F019.teaching_text: Blocking both directions perpendicular to traffic makes three-point turns a narrow two-lane last resort.

sec07-card-sec07-F020.question_text: What signals and checks open the first leg of a three-point turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F020.teaching_text: Pulling right first buys maximum width and lets trailing cars pass before you swing left across the road.

sec07-card-sec07-F021.question_text: After crossing to the opposite curb in a three-point turn, how do you execute the middle reverse leg?
sec07-card-sec07-F021.teaching_text: Turning the wheel sharply right while backing swings your front nose toward your new travel direction.

sec07-card-sec07-F022.question_text: What gear, signal, and checks complete the final leg of a three-point turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F022.teaching_text: Fast rural traffic can crest a hill mid-maneuver, so recheck both ways before pulling away.

sec07-card-sec07-F023.question_text: What possibility should you anticipate from other road users at every intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F023.teaching_text: Red-light runners and distracted drivers blow controls daily, making defensive readiness your real shield.

sec07-card-sec07-F024.question_text: In what order do you scan when pulling out from a stop, and why look left twice?
sec07-card-sec07-F024.teaching_text: Traffic and cyclists from the left cross your front bumper first right as you release the brake.

sec07-card-sec07-F025.question_text: Why must you pause and check rather than flooring the gas the instant a light turns green?
sec07-card-sec07-F025.teaching_text: Late cross-street drivers trying to beat yellow collide hardest with jackrabbit green-light launches.

sec07-card-sec07-F026.question_text: Why should you never pull out in front of an oncoming car solely because its turn signal is flashing?
sec07-card-sec07-F026.teaching_text: Drivers forget blinkers on or signal for a driveway just past you, turning an early pull-out into a T-bone.

sec07-card-sec07-F027.question_text: How do you pick the right approach lane before entering a multilane roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F027.teaching_text: Choosing your lane before the yield line prevents dangerous mid-circle lane cuts.

sec07-card-sec07-F028.question_text: To which lanes must you yield when entering a multilane roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F028.teaching_text: Inner-lane cars spiraling toward an exit cross the outer lane path right past your entry.

sec07-card-sec07-F029.question_text: Once inside a multilane roundabout, what is the rule on changing lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F029.teaching_text: Curved geometry creates wide blind spots where mid-circle lane swaps sideswipe neighboring cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F030.question_text: Why must you never overtake or ride side-by-side with another vehicle inside a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F030.teaching_text: Long trailers track wide across lane stripes and need full two-lane clearance around tight central islands.

sec07-card-sec07-F031.question_text: What must you do if an emergency vehicle approaches before you have entered a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F031.teaching_text: Pulling right before the entry apron leaves the narrow curved circle open for wide fire apparatus.

sec07-card-sec07-F032.question_text: What must you do if an emergency vehicle approaches after you are already circulating inside a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F032.teaching_text: Stopping inside the narrow ring chokes the entire intersection and blocks the emergency unit behind you.

sec07-card-sec07-F033.question_text: How many feet away must traffic in any direction stop when a school bus flashes red lights or extends its stop arm?
sec07-card-sec07-F033.teaching_text: Unless separated by a physical divider, twenty-five feet gives crossing children clear sightlines past the bus hood.

sec07-card-sec07-F034.question_text: When may you start moving again after stopping for a school bus, and how should you proceed?
sec07-card-sec07-F034.teaching_text: Creeping slowly afterward catches late children darting back for a dropped backpack.

sec07-card-sec07-F035.question_text: Where must a parked vehicle sit along a rural highway?
sec07-card-sec07-F035.teaching_text: Leaving even two tires on rural asphalt sets up high-speed rear-end crashes around blind bends.

sec07-card-sec07-F036.question_text: If pulling completely off the road is impossible, what sight distance and passing clearance must remain?
sec07-card-sec07-F036.teaching_text: Two hundred feet of visibility each way gives fast rural traffic time to spot your car and pass safely.

sec07-card-sec07-F037.question_text: Can police tow an abandoned roadside vehicle even if it sits well clear of the travel lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F037.teaching_text: Long-abandoned shoulder cars distract passing motorists and block snowplows or emergency pull-offs.

sec07-card-sec07-F038.question_text: What three details belong on a windshield note if a disabled vehicle must sit roadside for several hours?
sec07-card-sec07-F038.teaching_text: Letting patrol officers know help is already arranged and how to reach you helps avoid an immediate tow.

sec07-card-sec07-F039.question_text: How should you position your vehicle relative to traffic and the curb when parking along a street?
sec07-card-sec07-F039.teaching_text: Tucking tight to the curb keeps side mirrors and doors clear of passing trucks and bike lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F040.question_text: What two ignition steps are required before leaving a vehicle unattended, plus one recommended habit?
sec07-card-sec07-F040.teaching_text: Leaving an idling unattended vehicle invites dangerous hill rollaways and opportunistic joyride thefts within seconds.

sec07-card-sec07-F041.question_text: How do you secure an automatic versus a manual transmission when parking, and what brake goes on?
sec07-card-sec07-F041.teaching_text: Setting the parking brake takes strain off transmission pawls and backs up manual gears on slopes.

sec07-card-sec07-F042.question_text: What rule governs opening the traffic-side door of a parked car?
sec07-card-sec07-F042.teaching_text: Flinging a driver door open blind knocks cyclists to the pavement or shears off against passing cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F043.question_text: What two visual clues should you check before picking a street parking spot?
sec07-card-sec07-F043.teaching_text: Painted curbs and time-limit signs flag tow zones or fire lanes even when space looks wide open.

sec07-card-sec07-F044.question_text: Are the striped access aisles next to accessible parking spaces also protected by parking fines?
sec07-card-sec07-F044.teaching_text: Straddling the painted stripes blocks wheelchair lifts just as badly as taking the space itself.

sec07-card-sec07-F045.question_text: What equipment uses an accessible parking aisle, and how much of its painted width may be needed?
sec07-card-sec07-F045.teaching_text: Side-deploying van ramps fold all the way across the stripes before a wheelchair can roll off.

sec07-card-sec07-F046.question_text: Who should a driver or passenger call immediately if an illegally parked car blocks their accessible aisle?
sec07-card-sec07-F046.teaching_text: Local officers can cite and tow a vehicle stranding a disabled citizen outside or inside their van.

sec07-card-sec07-F047.question_text: How can a person with a walking disability or their driver report an accessible-parking violator to local police?
sec07-card-sec07-F047.teaching_text: New Hampshire empowers affected citizens to document accessible-space abuse with photographic and sworn proof.

sec07-card-sec07-F048.question_text: Name five roadway or pedestrian structures where parking is always prohibited?
sec07-card-sec07-F048.teaching_text: Double-parking or stopping on bridges, tunnels, sidewalks, or intersections chokes emergency and pedestrian flow.

sec07-card-sec07-F049.question_text: Why must you never park across a driveway, in a hazardous spot, or where lanes pinch narrow?
sec07-card-sec07-F049.teaching_text: Blocking property exits or pinching travel width traps homeowners and blocks wide fire trucks.

sec07-card-sec07-F050.question_text: How many feet must a parked vehicle stay from a fire hydrant versus an intersection crosswalk?
sec07-card-sec07-F050.teaching_text: Hose crews need fifteen feet around hydrants while twenty feet preserves corner pedestrian sightlines.

sec07-card-sec07-F051.question_text: How far must you stay parked from any stop sign, traffic light, or yield sign?
sec07-card-sec07-F051.teaching_text: Tall SUVs or vans parked closer than thirty feet hide corner stop signs from approaching drivers.

sec07-card-sec07-F052.question_text: How far from a fire-station driveway is parking banned on the station side versus across the street?
sec07-card-sec07-F052.teaching_text: Long ladder trucks swing wide across the opposite curb when turning out on emergency calls.

sec07-card-sec07-F053.question_text: How many feet from the nearest rail of a railroad crossing must parked vehicles stay clear?
sec07-card-sec07-F053.teaching_text: Keeping fifty feet open prevents parked vehicles from hiding warning flashers or approaching trains.

sec07-card-sec07-F054.question_text: What sequence of steps puts your car cleanly into an angled or perpendicular parking stall?
sec07-card-sec07-F054.teaching_text: Centering slowly between the lines gives neighboring cars room to open doors without dinging paint.

sec07-card-sec07-F055.question_text: When reversing out of an angled or perpendicular stall, when may you start turning the steering wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-F055.teaching_text: Cranking the wheel before your front bumper passes the car beside you scrapes its rear quarter panel.

sec07-card-sec07-F056.question_text: Once backed clear of a parking stall, how do you transition into forward travel?
sec07-card-sec07-F056.teaching_text: Coming to a dead stop before shifting from reverse to drive spares transmission gears and smooths takeoff.

sec07-card-sec07-F057.question_text: What four steps open a safe parallel parking maneuver?
sec07-card-sec07-F057.teaching_text: Signaling early tells trailing traffic to wait behind your space instead of pulling right onto your bumper.

sec07-card-sec07-F058.question_text: How do you finish positioning your car inside a parallel space without bumping the car behind you?
sec07-card-sec07-F058.teaching_text: Stopping short of the rear bumper and straightening forward centers your car evenly between both neighbors.

sec07-card-sec07-F059.question_text: What checks and initial move prepare you to pull out of a tight parallel parking space?
sec07-card-sec07-F059.teaching_text: Backing slightly first opens the front swing angle needed to clear the bumper parked ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-F060.question_text: What two essentials apply as you pull forward out of a parallel parking space into traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F060.teaching_text: Signaling alerts passing traffic while watching your right front corner avoids clipping the parked car ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-F001.question_text: Which four zones must a repeatable visual-search routine cover before you change direction?
sec08-card-sec08-F001.teaching_text: Cycling methodically through all four zones stops tunnel vision before lane swaps or turns.

sec08-card-sec08-F002.question_text: What head-and-eye habit must happen before your hands turn the steering wheel?
sec08-card-sec08-F002.teaching_text: Waiting until the nose swings into a corner discovers crosswalk walkers or stalled cars far too late.

sec08-card-sec08-F003.question_text: What two tactical options does continual eye movement buy you when hazards develop?
sec08-card-sec08-F003.teaching_text: Staring fixed at one bumper freezes reaction time, whereas active scanning lets you adjust smoothly early.

sec08-card-sec08-F004.question_text: How far ahead should your forward scan reach, and what habit pairs with it?
sec08-card-sec08-F004.teaching_text: Watching brake lights three cars ahead plus frequent mirror sweeps prevents chain-reaction surprises.

sec08-card-sec08-F005.question_text: Why is tailgating a large truck or bus blinding, and how do you fix your sightline?
sec08-card-sec08-F005.teaching_text: Wide box trailers wall off traffic signals, debris, and slowing lanes ahead until you open space.

sec08-card-sec08-F006.question_text: What are you watching for when scanning sidewalks, driveways, and side streets?
sec08-card-sec08-F006.teaching_text: Kids, cyclists, and nose-out cars telegraph side entry seconds before crossing your bumper.

sec08-card-sec08-F007.question_text: Before which four everyday actions is checking your rearview mirrors extra critical?
sec08-card-sec08-F007.teaching_text: Knowing whether a heavy truck or tailgater sits right off your trunk shapes how gently you brake.

sec08-card-sec08-F008.question_text: What primary advantage does keeping a larger cushion from other road users give you?
sec08-card-sec08-F008.teaching_text: Extra feet translate directly into calm seconds to steer or brake when someone ahead makes a mistake.

sec08-card-sec08-F009.question_text: Which five changing road and environment factors determine how much space cushion your car needs?
sec08-card-sec08-F009.teaching_text: A gap that works on dry noon pavement shrinks dangerously once dusk, rain, or highway speeds arrive.

sec08-card-sec08-F010.question_text: A proper forward following cushion gives you room to execute which two crash-avoidance moves?
sec08-card-sec08-F010.teaching_text: Sitting right on a bumper locks out steering around a sudden wreck as well as braking short.

sec08-card-sec08-F011.question_text: In what two ways does following too closely hurt your ability to avoid a crash?
sec08-card-sec08-F011.teaching_text: Blinding yourself behind a trunk lid while simultaneously halving reaction seconds guarantees rear-end hits.

sec08-card-sec08-F012.question_text: What minimum following interval in seconds does the New Hampshire handbook recommend?
sec08-card-sec08-F012.teaching_text: Unlike older two-second rules of thumb, New Hampshire tests four full seconds as your standard cushion.

sec08-card-sec08-F013.question_text: What exact moment triggers starting your four-second count when measuring following distance?
sec08-card-sec08-F013.teaching_text: Using a stationary pole, shadow, or sign post measures true travel time regardless of highway speed.

sec08-card-sec08-F014.question_text: When may your vehicle reach the fixed landmark during a four-second following check?
sec08-card-sec08-F014.teaching_text: Passing the pole on two or three proves you are riding inside your minimum stopping margin.

sec08-card-sec08-F015.question_text: What should you do if your front bumper reaches the landmark before four seconds finish?
sec08-card-sec08-F015.teaching_text: Gently backing off the throttle and re-timing at the next post verifies a true four-second buffer.

sec08-card-sec08-F016.question_text: How can you practice judging safe following intervals accurately on everyday drives?
sec08-card-sec08-F016.teaching_text: Comparing your visual estimate against a real four-count trains your eyes to spot close gaps instantly.

sec08-card-sec08-F017.question_text: Why must you stretch your forward following gap beyond four seconds on slippery pavement?
sec08-card-sec08-F017.teaching_text: Wet leaves, slush, and black ice multiply braking rollout long after your foot hits the pedal.

sec08-card-sec08-F018.question_text: Behind which four heavy or long vehicle types should you add extra following space?
sec08-card-sec08-F018.teaching_text: Wide bodies block forward sightlines, kick road spray, and need room if they roll slightly on grades.

sec08-card-sec08-F019.question_text: When lighting or weather deteriorates, how must your forward cushion change?
sec08-card-sec08-F019.teaching_text: Shorter headlight preview and rain glare delay spotting stopped cars until much closer.

sec08-card-sec08-F020.question_text: Why should you leave extra space behind school buses, transit buses, and hazmat carriers near railroad tracks?
sec08-card-sec08-F020.teaching_text: Those vehicles must halt at tracks even when crossing bells stay silent and gates stay up.

sec08-card-sec08-F021.question_text: Why is preserving open space to the left or right of your vehicle so valuable?
sec08-card-sec08-F021.teaching_text: When pavement turns slick or a lead car spins, an open side lane beats panic-braking straight into impact.

sec08-card-sec08-F022.question_text: What two hazards come from cruising side-by-side next to another vehicle for a long stretch?
sec08-card-sec08-F022.teaching_text: Drop back slightly or finish passing briskly so you never camp invisible off someone's rear fender.

sec08-card-sec08-F023.question_text: How should you position your car relative to the centerline on a two-way street?
sec08-card-sec08-F023.teaching_text: Every extra foot away from yellow paint widens your margin against distracted oncoming drifters.

sec08-card-sec08-F024.question_text: How can you help entering drivers join a multilane or limited-access highway smoothly?
sec08-card-sec08-F024.teaching_text: Moving left when clear or easing speed slightly prevents awkward side-by-side ramp conflicts.

sec08-card-sec08-F025.question_text: Around which vulnerable road users must you leave generous stopping and side clearance?
sec08-card-sec08-F025.teaching_text: Unprotected riders and children can wobble, trip, or swerve around a pothole without a second's notice.

sec08-card-sec08-F026.question_text: How do you give extra clearance to an approaching large truck or any vehicle rounding a curve?
sec08-card-sec08-F026.teaching_text: Long wheelbases and cornering momentum pull trailers and oncoming noses close to center paint on bends.

sec08-card-sec08-F027.question_text: Which three habits of yours help keep safer spacing behind your own rear bumper?
sec08-card-sec08-F027.teaching_text: Leaving extra room ahead lets you feather brakes gently so close followers behind you never panic-slam.

sec10-card-sec10-F001.question_text: Why should you think through a driving emergency before reacting?
sec10-card-sec10-F001.teaching_text: Impulsive wheel jerks or pedal slams turn recoverable mechanical or traction hiccups into rollovers and spinouts.

sec10-card-sec10-F002.question_text: What key control advantage does anti-lock braking preserve, and where should you check its instructions?
sec10-card-sec10-F002.teaching_text: Keeping front tires rolling instead of skidding lets you steer around hazards while braking according to your manual.

sec10-card-sec10-F003.question_text: How must you apply the brake pedal so an anti-lock braking system keeps working?
sec10-card-sec10-F003.teaching_text: Lifting off or pumping an anti-lock pedal interrupts computer modulation and lengthens your emergency stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F004.question_text: What do pedal vibration and clicking noises mean when braking hard with ABS?
sec10-card-sec10-F004.teaching_text: Startled drivers sometimes let go when the pedal chatters, not realizing that pulsing and clicking mean ABS is active.

sec10-card-sec10-F005.question_text: How should you find out the proper emergency braking method for a vehicle without anti-lock brakes?
sec10-card-sec10-F005.teaching_text: Older or specialty vehicles lacking anti-lock systems require threshold or controlled braking steps detailed in the owner's manual.

sec10-card-sec10-F006.question_text: How can an evasive steering maneuver prevent a crash when braking space runs short?
sec10-card-sec10-F006.teaching_text: At highway speeds a car can often swerve clear of a lane obstacle in far less distance than stopping takes.

sec10-card-sec10-F007.question_text: How should you hold the wheel and which direction must you avoid when dodging an oncoming vehicle?
sec10-card-sec10-F007.teaching_text: Swerving left into the opposing lane risks a head-on crash the moment the drifting driver snaps back into place.

sec10-card-sec10-F008.question_text: What steering step follows right after an evasive maneuver clears an obstacle?
sec10-card-sec10-F008.teaching_text: Without steering smoothly back the opposite way once clear, your evasive move carries you off the shoulder.

sec10-card-sec10-F009.question_text: Against which specific collision threats can accelerating help instead of making things worse?
sec10-card-sec10-F009.teaching_text: Speeding up worsens front hazards, yet brisk throttle can pull you clear of an intersection broadside or rear-ender.

sec10-card-sec10-F010.question_text: Which three driving or traction triggers commonly start a skid and strip vehicle control?
sec10-card-sec10-F010.teaching_text: Outrunning surface conditions, slamming the brakes, or hitting slick patches breaks tire bite and leaves minimal control.

sec10-card-sec10-F011.question_text: How should you adjust the gas pedal and steering wheel if your vehicle begins to skid?
sec10-card-sec10-F011.teaching_text: Lifting smoothly off the accelerator while pointing front wheels toward the sliding tail brings the chassis back inline.

sec10-card-sec10-F012.question_text: What must you stay ready for if a skid whips the other way, and what do you do once traction returns?
sec10-card-sec10-F012.teaching_text: Holding recovery lock too long causes a fishtail snap the opposite way unless you countersteer and straighten promptly.

sec10-card-sec10-F013.question_text: How should you recover if your tires drop off the paved edge onto the shoulder?
sec10-card-sec10-F013.teaching_text: Jerking back at highway speed catches the asphalt lip and spins you across oncoming lanes, so slow gradually first.

sec10-card-sec10-F014.question_text: What routine habit lowers the chance of suffering a sudden mechanical failure on the road?
sec10-card-sec10-F014.teaching_text: Keeping up with scheduled belt, brake, fluid, and tire service catches worn parts long before highway failure.

sec10-card-sec10-F015.question_text: Which two conditions does the handbook highlight as causes of lost braking ability?
sec10-card-sec10-F015.teaching_text: Driving through deep puddles soaks rotors and linings with water that temporarily kills friction just like hardware failure.

sec10-card-sec10-F016.question_text: How should you apply a hand or foot parking brake if your primary service brakes fail?
sec10-card-sec10-F016.teaching_text: Yanking or stomping the parking brake all at once locks the rear tires solid instead of slowing smoothly.

sec10-card-sec10-F017.question_text: What must you stay ready to do if applying the parking brake starts a rear-wheel skid?
sec10-card-sec10-F017.teaching_text: Keeping thumb or release control ready lets you back off cable tension instantly if the rear end slides.

sec10-card-sec10-F018.question_text: How does a front tire blowout feel at the wheel compared with a rear tire blowout?
sec10-card-sec10-F018.teaching_text: Front blowouts yank steering strongly toward the flat side, whereas rear blowouts shake and wobble the tail.

sec10-card-sec10-F019.question_text: What steering and gas-pedal actions apply right when a tire blows out?
sec10-card-sec10-F019.teaching_text: Fighting the pull with a firm two-hand grip while easing off throttle keeps weight balanced without brake-lock spin.

sec10-card-sec10-F020.question_text: How should you bring a car with a blown tire to a roadside stop and mark it?
sec10-card-sec10-F020.teaching_text: Letting rolling resistance bleed speed before gentle braking guides you safely off-road with hazard flashers warning traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F021.question_text: Why must you keep a firm grip on the steering wheel if the engine dies while moving?
sec10-card-sec10-F021.teaching_text: Power-steering assist drops out when the engine stalls, requiring much stronger arm effort to turn the wheel.

sec10-card-sec10-F022.question_text: How should you use the brakes and position the car after losing engine power?
sec10-card-sec10-F022.teaching_text: Vacuum brake boost runs out if you pump repeatedly, so apply one steady press while steering off the road.

sec10-card-sec10-F023.question_text: Once safely stopped after engine power loss, what sequence should you follow?
sec10-card-sec10-F023.teaching_text: If a safe restart attempt fails, raising the hood and running warning flashers signals trouble while calling help.

sec10-card-sec10-F024.question_text: What three immediate steps counter a stuck accelerator while keeping control on the road?
sec10-card-sec10-F024.teaching_text: Shifting into Neutral disconnects runaway engine power from the wheels immediately while firm braking slows the car.

sec10-card-sec10-F025.question_text: With a stuck accelerator, when do you turn the engine off?
sec10-card-sec10-F025.teaching_text: Turning the key off while still rolling kills power steering and can lock the steering column mid-maneuver.

sec10-card-sec10-F026.question_text: Which backup lights can help if your headlights suddenly go dark, and what should you do?
sec10-card-sec10-F026.teaching_text: Turn indicators or hazard flashers cast enough emergency glow to guide you off the pavement and mark your position.

sec10-card-sec10-F027.question_text: What are your first lighting and positioning steps during a vehicle breakdown?
sec10-card-sec10-F027.teaching_text: Switching hazard lamps on right away alerts trailing drivers while momentum still carries you clear of travel lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F028.question_text: Where does the New Hampshire manual say to place reflectors or flares around a disabled vehicle?
sec10-card-sec10-F028.teaching_text: Watch both directions on exam questions because New Hampshire places markers two hundred feet ahead and behind.

sec10-card-sec10-F029.question_text: Once your disabled vehicle is safely stopped, how should you summon assistance?
sec10-card-sec10-F029.teaching_text: Alerting authorities from your stopped vehicle brings patrol or tow support without risking a walk along highway shoulders.

sec10-card-sec10-F030.question_text: With no phone available, how do you signal for help normally versus during a snowstorm?
sec10-card-sec10-F030.teaching_text: A white cloth blends right into blowing snow, so snowstorms swap to a bright red cloth on handle or antenna.

sec10-card-sec10-F031.question_text: When should occupants stay inside a disabled vehicle versus leaving it?
sec10-card-sec10-F031.teaching_text: Remaining with the car helps rescuers find you, unless stopping in an exposed spot forces everyone well clear.

sec11-card-sec11-F001.question_text: Alongside passenger cars, which five groups of travelers share New Hampshire roadways?
sec11-card-sec11-F001.teaching_text: Expecting everything from pedestrians and bikes to heavy rigs, animal riders, and slow farm gear prevents tunnel vision.

sec11-card-sec11-F002.question_text: Around which four neighborhood spots must you use exceptional pedestrian care and stay ready to yield?
sec11-card-sec11-F002.teaching_text: Distracted kids dart unpredictably around schoolyards, bus stops, parks, and playgrounds without checking approaching cars.

sec11-card-sec11-F003.question_text: Where do pedestrians hold statutory right-of-way at intersections and mid-block entrances?
sec11-card-sec11-F003.teaching_text: Pulling into or out of a driveway or alley never overrides a pedestrian continuing along the crossing sidewalk.

sec11-card-sec11-F004.question_text: What three crossing habits should pedestrians follow at intersections?
sec11-card-sec11-F004.teaching_text: Crossing inside marked lines, following walk signals, and checking both directions keeps pedestrians predictable to turning traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F005.question_text: On which side of the road should a pedestrian walk when no sidewalk exists?
sec11-card-sec11-F005.teaching_text: Facing oncoming cars lets walkers see approaching vehicles directly and step aside instead of trusting traffic behind their backs.

sec11-card-sec11-F006.question_text: How should pedestrians stay visible after dark, and on which highways is walking banned?
sec11-card-sec11-F006.teaching_text: Light clothing or flashlights help drivers spot walkers early, while high-speed interstates and limited-access roads ban foot travel.

sec11-card-sec11-F007.question_text: What two pedestrian checks apply around parked vehicles and before shifting into Reverse?
sec11-card-sec11-F007.teaching_text: Small children and shoppers step out from between parked SUVs unseen unless you scan gaps and check behind first.

sec11-card-sec11-F008.question_text: When must you obey reduced school-zone speeds, and how do you respond to a crossing guard?
sec11-card-sec11-F008.teaching_text: Visible children or flashing school beacons activate lower limits immediately, and a crossing guard's stop signal is mandatory.

sec11-card-sec11-F009.question_text: What must you do when a pedestrian with a white cane or harnessed guide dog prepares to cross?
sec11-card-sec11-F009.teaching_text: Rolling slowly past a blind pedestrian violates white-cane protection because you must come to a complete halt first.

sec11-card-sec11-F010.question_text: Why must you never honk or shout at a visually impaired pedestrian waiting to cross?
sec11-card-sec11-F010.teaching_text: Blind pedestrians listen carefully for your stopped vehicle's sound cues, and horn blasts or shouting Mask traffic direction.

sec11-card-sec11-F011.question_text: How does New Hampshire traffic law classify bicycles riding on the roadway?
sec11-card-sec11-F011.teaching_text: Bicyclists hold the exact same legal roadway rights, privileges, and rule obligations as motor-vehicle operators.

sec11-card-sec11-F012.question_text: What minimum passing clearance applies around a bicycle when traffic moves at thirty miles per hour or less?
sec11-card-sec11-F012.teaching_text: Giving at least three feet of side buffer at city speeds prevents mirror clips and wind-blast wobbles.

sec11-card-sec11-F013.question_text: How does New Hampshire's bicycle-passing buffer increase at speeds above thirty miles per hour?
sec11-card-sec11-F013.teaching_text: Faster wind wash needs wider room, demanding four feet at forty miles per hour and five feet at fifty.

sec11-card-sec11-F014.question_text: Where must motorists yield to bicyclists at junctions and trail crossings?
sec11-card-sec11-F014.teaching_text: Treat intersecting bike lanes and multi-use path crossings with full intersection yielding awareness before rolling across.

sec11-card-sec11-F015.question_text: May you drive, stop, or park in a marked bike lane, and what narrow exceptions exist?
sec11-card-sec11-F015.teaching_text: Blocking a bike lane forces cyclists into fast cars, allowed only for driveway access, police direction, emergencies, or authorized duty.

sec11-card-sec11-F016.question_text: How should you pass a bicyclist near an intersection where you plan to turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F016.teaching_text: Overtaking a cyclist only to cut right across their nose causes classic right-hook crashes, so let them clear first.

sec11-card-sec11-F017.question_text: Why must you avoid sudden braking right after pulling ahead of a bicycle?
sec11-card-sec11-F017.teaching_text: Four wide car tires shed speed much faster than two thin bicycle tires, causing rear-end collisions if you slam brakes.

sec11-card-sec11-F018.question_text: When is sounding your horn near a bicyclist allowed, and why skip friendly taps?
sec11-card-sec11-F018.teaching_text: A sudden loud blast right behind a cyclist can startle them into swerving straight into your front fender.

sec11-card-sec11-F019.question_text: Which young riders require special vigilance along residential curbs and sidewalks?
sec11-card-sec11-F019.teaching_text: Young cyclists often roll down driveway aprons from sidewalks into the street without looking back over their shoulders.

sec11-card-sec11-F020.question_text: What two aggressive lane or turning moves are strictly off-limits around a bicyclist?
sec11-card-sec11-F020.teaching_text: Turning sharply across a bike's line or squeezing a rider onto loose shoulder gravel leaves zero escape room.

sec11-card-sec11-F021.question_text: Should you scan only the right curb for bicycles traveling with traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-F021.teaching_text: Even though cyclists must ride with traffic flow, scanning both directions catches wrong-way riders before you pull out.

sec11-card-sec11-F022.question_text: Which three road-surface conditions hit two-wheeled bicycles especially hard?
sec11-card-sec11-F022.teaching_text: Slick puddles, winter sand, or loose shoulder gravel can wash out a skinny front bicycle tire instantly.

sec11-card-sec11-F023.question_text: Why might a cyclist skip a hand signal, and what body clues foretell a turn or lane move?
sec11-card-sec11-F023.teaching_text: Braking or rough pavement requires both hands on handlebars, making a rider's head turn or shoulder glance your warning.

sec11-card-sec11-F024.question_text: What check must you make before swinging open a parked car's door or backing near homes and schools?
sec11-card-sec11-F024.teaching_text: Flinging a street-side door open into an oncoming cyclist causes severe crashes that a quick mirror-and-shoulder check prevents.

sec11-card-sec11-F025.question_text: Why are motorcycles harder to spot and judge in traffic despite sharing full driver rights?
sec11-card-sec11-F025.teaching_text: A slim silhouette disappears easily behind windshield pillars or mirrors and makes oncoming bikes look farther away.

sec11-card-sec11-F026.question_text: How much of a traffic lane belongs to a motorcycle, and may a car share side-by-side?
sec11-card-sec11-F026.teaching_text: Riders shift across the full lane width to dodge potholes, oil streaks, and wind gusts, leaving zero sharing room.

sec11-card-sec11-F027.question_text: What must you check extra carefully before turning left across oncoming traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-F027.teaching_text: Left-turning cars misjudging a single approaching headlamp cause one of the deadliest intersection motorcycle crashes.

sec11-card-sec11-F028.question_text: At least how much following time should you maintain behind a motorcycle?
sec11-card-sec11-F028.teaching_text: Motorcycles can downshift or stop rapidly without brake lights flashing first, demanding a four-second cushion behind them.

sec11-card-sec11-F029.question_text: Why shouldn't you pull out based solely on a motorcycle's blinking turn signal?
sec11-card-sec11-F029.teaching_text: Many motorcycle turn signals do not self-cancel after lane changes, so confirm the rider slows and leans first.

sec11-card-sec11-F030.question_text: How do foul weather, slick pavement, and wet nighttime glare affect motorcyclists?
sec11-card-sec11-F030.teaching_text: Slippery rain forces riders to adjust speed or line suddenly while wet-asphalt reflections make spotting bikes harder.

sec11-card-sec11-F031.question_text: Where can crosswinds and passing truck air blasts push a motorcycle sideways?
sec11-card-sec11-F031.teaching_text: Open highway stretches and exposed bridges amplify crosswinds and semi-truck bow waves that nudge lightweight bikes laterally.

sec11-card-sec11-F032.question_text: How do road seams, gravel, manhole covers, and grated metal bridges affect motorcycles?
sec11-card-sec11-F032.teaching_text: Pavement grooves, debris, and steel bridge grates make two-wheeled tires wander or wobble, so leave extra room.

sec11-card-sec11-F033.question_text: What rear sign marks animal-drawn, farm, or construction equipment moving under twenty-five miles per hour?
sec11-card-sec11-F033.teaching_text: Spotting that fluorescent orange-and-red triangle ahead warns you to shed highway speed immediately because closing distance vanishes fast.

sec11-card-sec11-F034.question_text: How should you approach and pass a slow-moving vehicle on the road?
sec11-card-sec11-F034.teaching_text: Wide farm or construction gear often turns left into unmarked field gates just as impatient drivers swing out.

sec11-card-sec11-F035.question_text: What should you watch for on rural roads, and why shouldn't you assume a tractor operator hears you?
sec11-card-sec11-F035.teaching_text: Heavy diesel engines and implement clatter drown out approaching cars and horns while machinery crosses rural highways.

sec11-card-sec11-F036.question_text: What roadway status applies to horse riders and animal-drawn vehicles in New Hampshire?
sec11-card-sec11-F036.teaching_text: Equestrians and horse-drawn carriages hold legitimate roadway access alongside full traffic-law responsibilities on shared public roads.

sec11-card-sec11-F037.question_text: How must you pass a horse on the road, and which two noises are off-limits?
sec11-card-sec11-F037.teaching_text: Honking or revving your exhaust can spook a thousand-pound horse into bolting sideways into your windshield.

sec11-card-sec11-F038.question_text: In what three ways do large commercial trucks handle differently than passenger cars?
sec11-card-sec11-F038.teaching_text: Heavy rigs carry wider blind zones and take far more pavement both to build speed and to haul down.

sec11-card-sec11-F039.question_text: Why must you leave extra intersection clearance around a turning truck or bus?
sec11-card-sec11-F039.teaching_text: Rear trailer wheels track tighter inside the cab's arc, needing extra lane width to clear corners cleanly.

sec11-card-sec11-F040.question_text: What does the term No-Zone refer to around a large truck or bus?
sec11-card-sec11-F040.teaching_text: Lingering in the front, tail, or side No-Zones hides your entire car from the commercial driver's sightlines.

sec11-card-sec11-F041.question_text: How far does a truck's right-side blind spot stretch, and how should you handle driving beside it?
sec11-card-sec11-F041.teaching_text: The right-side No-Zone runs from behind the cab down the whole trailer, so never cruise alongside a semi.

sec11-card-sec11-F042.question_text: How can you tell instantly whether a truck driver can see your car in their side mirror?
sec11-card-sec11-F042.teaching_text: If you cannot spot the trucker's face reflected in their side mirror, light physics guarantees they cannot see you.

sec11-card-sec11-F043.question_text: Under ideal conditions at fifty-five miles per hour, at least how many feet does a loaded truck need to stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F043.teaching_text: Even dry pavement and fresh brakes need deeper than a football field to stop a loaded fifty-five-mile-an-hour semi.

sec11-card-sec11-F044.question_text: Why must you avoid pulling out or merging closely ahead of a large truck?
sec11-card-sec11-F044.teaching_text: Slicing into a truck's front cushion steals the hundreds of feet its driver needs if traffic ahead brakes.

sec11-card-sec11-F045.question_text: After overtaking a large truck, what mirror cue tells you it is safe to merge back ahead and hold speed?
sec11-card-sec11-F045.teaching_text: Seeing the entire cab grill in your interior mirror confirms safe bumper clearance so you never force hard braking.

sec11-card-sec11-F046.question_text: How far behind a large vehicle can its rear blind spot reach, and where should you position instead?
sec11-card-sec11-F046.teaching_text: Tailgating within two hundred feet blocks both your forward traffic view and the trucker's mirror view of you.

sec11-card-sec11-F047.question_text: Why should you leave the right lane open near weigh-station exits and steep highway grades when practical?
sec11-card-sec11-F047.teaching_text: Heavy rigs merge out of scales slowly and lose speed climbing hills, needing clear right-lane space.

sec11-card-sec11-F048.question_text: Why might a truck swing left before turning right, and what curb mistake must you never make?
sec11-card-sec11-F048.teaching_text: Sneaking into the open gap between a wide-swinging trailer and the right curb crushes cars as the trailer tracks.

sec11-card-sec11-F049.question_text: How should you respond while a large vehicle is swinging wide through an intersection turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F049.teaching_text: Trying to dart around a mid-turn bus or trailer puts your car inside sweeping blind overhangs.

sec11-card-sec11-F050.question_text: Where should you position in your lane when meeting an oncoming truck, and why?
sec11-card-sec11-F050.teaching_text: Hugging the right side buffers mirror-to-mirror clearance and softens the air-turbulence buffet between passing vehicles.

sec11-card-sec11-F051.question_text: What should you do at a left turn if you aren't sure how fast an oncoming truck or bus is closing?
sec11-card-sec11-F051.teaching_text: Large vehicles often travel faster than their size suggests and cannot shed speed quickly if you misjudge.

sec11-card-sec11-F052.question_text: Why is stopping behind the painted white stop line especially important around large vehicles?
sec11-card-sec11-F052.teaching_text: Creeping past the white line blocks the corner arc engineered for long trucks and buses turning into your street.

sec11-card-sec11-F053.question_text: Why must you never dart ahead of a large truck to catch an exit or beat a single-lane work taper?
sec11-card-sec11-F053.teaching_text: Diving across a truck's nose at an exit ramp or construction squeeze leaves zero room for heavy brakes.

sec11-card-sec11-F054.question_text: How must you yield when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren from any direction?
sec11-card-sec11-F054.teaching_text: Pulling to the right edge and stopping outside intersections keeps cross streets open for turning ambulances or engines.

sec11-card-sec11-F055.question_text: What two steps apply before pulling back into traffic after an emergency vehicle passes?
sec11-card-sec11-F055.teaching_text: Checking mirrors for a trailing second responder and signaling prevents pulling straight into another fast unit.

sec11-card-sec11-F056.question_text: How far back must you stay behind a responding fire truck, and where is driving or parking barred at a fire?
sec11-card-sec11-F056.teaching_text: Staying five hundred feet back and out of the alarm block keeps hydrants, hoses, and ladder rigs unobstructed.

sec11-card-sec11-F057.question_text: How must you adjust speed and spacing past a highway emergency, police stop, or flashing roadside vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F057.teaching_text: Dropping speed and giving wide clearance shields roadside troopers, tow operators, and stranded drivers without crowding opposing traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F058.question_text: When traffic allows on a multi-lane road, how should you position lanes near emergency personnel or blocked lanes?
sec11-card-sec11-F058.teaching_text: Shifting a full lane away from responders and clearing partly blocked lanes early prevents last-moment swerves.

sec11-card-sec11-F059.question_text: Whose instructions govern traffic around a crash, fire, maintenance crew, or roadway emergency?
sec11-card-sec11-F059.teaching_text: Live hand directions and emergency flares override ordinary lane habits when crews reroute traffic around active scenes.

sec11-card-sec11-F060.question_text: What penalty hits a move-over violation, and what lookback window triggers a steeper repeat fine?
sec11-card-sec11-F060.teaching_text: Ignoring move-over duties brings a fine and penalty assessment that jumps higher on a repeat offense within twelve months.

sec11-card-sec11-F061.question_text: When pulled over by police, how do you position the car, shift gear, and handle staying inside?
sec11-card-sec11-F061.teaching_text: Shifting fully into Park prevents accidental roll while staying seated avoids alarming the approaching officer.

sec11-card-sec11-F062.question_text: During a police stop, what should you do with the engine, hazard flashers, and interior dome light at night?
sec11-card-sec11-F062.teaching_text: Turning off the engine, running hazards, and switching on the cabin light after dark shows calm transparency.

sec11-card-sec11-F063.question_text: Should you unbuckle right away during a traffic stop, or how should you and passengers sit?
sec11-card-sec11-F063.teaching_text: Unbuckling early looks like rummaging or exiting, so keep everyone belted and still with driver hands on the wheel.

sec11-card-sec11-F064.question_text: How should you retrieve your license and registration once the officer asks for them?
sec11-card-sec11-F064.teaching_text: Telling the officer where documents sit and reaching slowly with one hand still on the wheel keeps everything clear.

sec11-card-sec11-F065.question_text: What light color should an unmarked police car display, and what can you request from a plainclothes officer?
sec11-card-sec11-F065.teaching_text: New Hampshire law enforcement runs blue emergency lights, and plainclothes officers carry a department badge or police ID.

sec11-card-sec11-F066.question_text: What lane, surface, and activity changes make construction work zones hazardous?
sec11-card-sec11-F066.teaching_text: Shifting detours, closed lanes, uneven milled asphalt, and heavy equipment moving near crews leave little error margin.

sec11-card-sec11-F067.question_text: Should you slow down in an orange-marked work zone even if no lower speed limit is posted?
sec11-card-sec11-F067.teaching_text: Orange signs, cones, barrels, trucks, and crews signal tight clearance where slowing down protects lives without a new sign.

sec11-card-sec11-F068.question_text: How should you adjust your following gap and brake readiness inside a construction zone?
sec11-card-sec11-F068.teaching_text: Rear-end collisions are the top work-zone crash type when tailgaters get caught by sudden flagger stops.

sec11-card-sec11-F069.question_text: How should you drive through a work zone at night when no workers appear present?
sec11-card-sec11-F069.teaching_text: Shifted Jersey barriers, lane drops, barrels, and pavement ledges remain just as hazardous after crews clock out.

sec11-card-sec11-F070.question_text: How should you position within your lane and follow signs past road workers and equipment?
sec11-card-sec11-F070.teaching_text: Tracking slightly away from cones and obeying posted lane instructions builds lifelines for workers inches away.

sec11-card-sec11-F071.question_text: When may you accelerate back up to normal highway speed after passing construction?
sec11-card-sec11-F071.teaching_text: Speeding up as soon as cones thin out is premature until the End Road Work marker comes into view.

sec11-card-sec11-F072.question_text: What three trip-planning habits reduce frustration around known construction zones?
sec11-card-sec11-F072.teaching_text: Starting earlier or picking an alternate route beats rushing impatiently through narrow construction chutes.

sec03-card-sec03-F001.question_text: How can poor vision hurt driving performance, and what preventative step does the handbook recommend?
sec03-card-sec03-F001.teaching_text: Unchecked vision changes delay spotting traffic cues and hazards, making periodic eye exams essential for safe reaction times.

sec03-card-sec03-F002.question_text: What two rules apply to drivers who require corrective lenses, especially when driving after dark?
sec03-card-sec03-F002.teaching_text: Prescription glasses must stay on while driving, yet dark or tinted lenses at night starve your eyes of dim contrast.

sec03-card-sec03-F003.question_text: How does the handbook define fatigue, and what common causes bring it on?
sec03-card-sec03-F003.teaching_text: Fatigue goes beyond mild sleepiness, arising from short sleep, illness, heavy exertion, or monotonous highway miles.

sec03-card-sec03-F004.question_text: Which two critical driving abilities suffer when you are tired, and what should you do?
sec03-card-sec03-F004.teaching_text: Heavy eyelids degrade visual tracking and stall split-second choices, leaving staying off the road as the safe call.

sec03-card-sec03-F005.question_text: To what impairment does the handbook compare extended wakefulness, and who carries responsibility to prevent it?
sec03-card-sec03-F005.teaching_text: Staying awake too long degrades coordination and reaction much like alcohol, putting full preventive responsibility on the driver.

sec03-card-sec03-F006.question_text: What average nightly sleep range does the manual recommend for ordinary daytime alertness?
sec03-card-sec03-F006.teaching_text: Starting a road trip well rested with seven to nine hours of sleep prevents mid-afternoon highway microsleeps.

sec03-card-sec03-F007.question_text: How often should you schedule a rest break during a long drive?
sec03-card-sec03-F007.teaching_text: Stepping out to stretch and hydrate every two hours resets focus before highway hypnosis creeps up on you.

sec03-card-sec03-F008.question_text: What should you do at an exit or rest area before drowsiness becomes severe?
sec03-card-sec03-F008.teaching_text: Pulling into a rest stop for a brief fifteen-to-twenty-minute nap or booking a room beats fighting closing eyelids.

sec03-card-sec03-F009.question_text: Which two scheduling and passenger habits help prevent drowsy driving on longer trips?
sec03-card-sec03-F009.teaching_text: Planning travel during normal waking hours and rotating driving shifts with a companion keeps fresh eyes on traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F010.question_text: What three types of inattention make up driving distraction and raise crash risk?
sec03-card-sec03-F010.teaching_text: Looking away, lifting hands off the wheel, or daydreaming mentally can each trigger a collision in heartbeats.

sec03-card-sec03-F011.question_text: Does New Hampshire's handheld-electronics ban apply only while rolling, or during traffic stops too?
sec03-card-sec03-F011.teaching_text: Drivers get ticketed at red lights because the handheld ban covers brief traffic and signal stops alongside moving travel.

sec03-card-sec03-F012.question_text: Which handheld phone and portable-device actions are prohibited behind the wheel?
sec03-card-sec03-F012.teaching_text: Typing an address into navigation or browsing data steals visual attention just as dangerously as texting or calling.

sec03-card-sec03-F013.question_text: What legal presumption arises when a driver holds a voice-capable device beside their ear in a moving car?
sec03-card-sec03-F013.teaching_text: Claiming you were not actively talking rarely works because holding a phone near your ear creates a calling presumption.

sec03-card-sec03-F014.question_text: What mobile-electronics rule applies to drivers under eighteen while driving or stopped in traffic?
sec03-card-sec03-F014.teaching_text: Adult Bluetooth permissions do not extend to minors, leaving emergency calls to dispatch or public safety as the sole exception.

sec03-card-sec03-F015.question_text: How does permitted hands-free equipment work, and what limited hand touch does the rule allow?
sec03-card-sec03-F015.teaching_text: Adult drivers may use one hand briefly to start, activate, or end a feature without holding the device during conversation.

sec03-card-sec03-F016.question_text: Even when hands-free use is permitted, where must the driver's attention stay?
sec03-card-sec03-F016.teaching_text: Bluetooth keeps fingers on the rim yet still risks cognitive distraction unless your focus stays locked on traffic ahead.

sec03-card-sec03-F017.question_text: What mandatory vehicle-compliance device is exempted under the electronics restrictions?
sec03-card-sec03-F017.teaching_text: Performing a required rolling breath prompt on an ignition interlock is explicitly carved out from the mobile-device ban.

sec03-card-sec03-F018.question_text: Which kinds of passenger conversations should you avoid while operating a vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F018.teaching_text: Heated debates inside the cabin hijack mental bandwidth and push drivers toward erratic speed and missed hazards.

sec03-card-sec03-F019.question_text: What rules cover eating while driving plus securing children and pets inside the vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F019.teaching_text: Unwrapping food, unbuckled kids, or loose pets climbing toward pedals can trigger sudden swerves in traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F020.question_text: Do noisy passengers or in-car gadgets shift responsibility away from the driver?
sec03-card-sec03-F020.teaching_text: No passenger distraction or dashboard screen excuses careless driving because legal responsibility always stays with the operator.

sec03-card-sec03-F021.question_text: How does the New Hampshire manual define aggressive driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F021.teaching_text: Crossing from a mistake into deliberate risk-taking that endangers others or their vehicles defines aggressive driving.

sec03-card-sec03-F022.question_text: Which five roadway behaviors does the manual highlight as aggressive driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F022.teaching_text: Combining excess speed, close following, abrupt lane cuts, skipped signals, and blown controls multiplies multi-car crash danger.

sec03-card-sec03-F023.question_text: What mindset and focus should you maintain toward driving and other road users?
sec03-card-sec03-F023.teaching_text: Giving fellow motorists space and grace prevents minor traffic friction from escalating into hostile confrontations.

sec03-card-sec03-F024.question_text: Which impairing substances are drivers under twenty-one barred from controlling a vehicle under?
sec03-card-sec03-F024.teaching_text: Underage zero-tolerance impairment rules reach beyond alcohol to controlled drugs, prescriptions, over-the-counter meds, and any impairing substance.

sec03-card-sec03-F025.question_text: What alcohol-concentration threshold triggers the under-twenty-one limit in New Hampshire?
sec03-card-sec03-F025.teaching_text: Hitting that trace underage threshold or higher brings Youth Operator sanctions even after a small amount of alcohol.

sec03-card-sec03-F026.question_text: When may a driver under twenty-one lawfully transport alcoholic beverages in a vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F026.teaching_text: Carrying unopened beer or wine solo under twenty-one violates transport law unless accompanied by a parent, guardian, or legal-age spouse.

sec03-card-sec03-F027.question_text: Which three core driving faculties do alcohol and other impairing substances weaken?
sec03-card-sec03-F027.teaching_text: Losing clear decisions, sharp eyesight, and brisk reflexes all at once leaves no backup skill to prevent a wreck.

sec03-card-sec03-F028.question_text: How does impaired judgment affect moment-to-moment driving performance?
sec03-card-sec03-F028.teaching_text: Hesitating or picking risky gaps at intersections happens because alcohol clouds rapid, accurate decision-making.

sec03-card-sec03-F029.question_text: What specific vision and depth-estimation problems can alcohol cause behind the wheel?
sec03-card-sec03-F029.teaching_text: Eye muscles relax under alcohol, causing sluggish focus, double images, and poor estimates of distance and closing speed.

sec03-card-sec03-F030.question_text: How does an impaired reaction slow a driver from hazard detection to vehicle control?
sec03-card-sec03-F030.teaching_text: Both mental recognition and physical foot movement lag behind, adding yards of extra travel before braking even begins.

sec03-card-sec03-F031.question_text: When does alcohol begin affecting driving ability, and what is the handbook's advice on drinking and driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F031.teaching_text: Impairment starts well below statutory limits with the very first drink, so never drive after alcohol or impairing drugs.

sec03-card-sec03-F032.question_text: What responsibility do you share when a friend or relative has been drinking or using an impairing drug?
sec03-card-sec03-F032.teaching_text: Stepping in to take keys or call a ride saves friends and strangers when impaired judgment tells someone they're fine.

sec03-card-sec03-F033.question_text: What actually reduces alcohol's effects, and what do coffee, food, exercise, or cold showers really do?
sec03-card-sec03-F033.teaching_text: Caffeine or cold water merely makes an intoxicated person feel more awake without lowering blood alcohol or restoring reflexes.

sec03-card-sec03-F034.question_text: How is an initial New Hampshire impaired-driving conviction classified, and what fine and suspension range apply?
sec03-card-sec03-F034.teaching_text: Even a first offense brings a criminal record, at least five hundred dollars in fines, and up to two years suspended.

sec03-card-sec03-F035.question_text: What educational requirement must be completed to restore privileges after an initial impaired-driving conviction?
sec03-card-sec03-F035.teaching_text: Serving out your suspension time and paying fines will not restore your license until you complete approved impaired-driver education.

sec03-card-sec03-F036.question_text: How do consequences change upon repeat impaired-driving convictions?
sec03-card-sec03-F036.teaching_text: Subsequent impaired-driving offenses escalate sharply with heavier financial fines and much longer license suspensions.

sec03-card-sec03-F037.question_text: How can nonprescription remedies for pain, colds, allergies, or nervousness affect a driver?
sec03-card-sec03-F037.teaching_text: Everyday allergy and cold tablets sold without a prescription often induce heavy sleepiness that degrades safe vehicle control.

sec03-card-sec03-F038.question_text: What side effects from stimulant or diet pills can interfere with safe driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F038.teaching_text: Taking stimulants to fight fatigue backfires when nervousness, dizzy spells, scattered focus, or visual disturbances hit mid-drive.

sec03-card-sec03-F039.question_text: What two checks should you perform before driving on an unfamiliar medication?
sec03-card-sec03-F039.teaching_text: Checking label warnings first and consulting your clinician or pharmacist prevents getting surprised by drowsiness on the highway.

sec03-card-sec03-F040.question_text: Which skills can prescription medicines impair, and what drug categories does the handbook highlight?
sec03-card-sec03-F040.teaching_text: Prescribed antidepressants, pain medicines, sleep aids, and sedatives can dull alertness, vision, judgment, and braking reflexes.

sec03-card-sec03-F041.question_text: How do illegal drugs affect driving, and what is the legal status of driving under their influence?
sec03-card-sec03-F041.teaching_text: Illicit substances distort perception and motor control, making drug-impaired driving both a serious crime and a crash hazard.

sec03-card-sec03-F042.question_text: Why must you avoid drinking alcohol while taking any other drugs or medications?
sec03-card-sec03-F042.teaching_text: Mixing alcohol with pills creates a multiplier effect that intensifies drowsiness and coordination loss far beyond expectation.

sec03-card-sec03-F043.question_text: How can strong emotions like anger, worry, fear, excitement, or depression affect driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F043.teaching_text: Even positive excitement or heavy worry preoccupies working memory and slows how quickly you spot changing traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F044.question_text: What should you do before driving while upset, and what two calming steps does the handbook suggest?
sec03-card-sec03-F044.teaching_text: Taking a brisk walk or short nap clears adrenaline and mental fog before you step behind the steering wheel.

sec03-card-sec03-F045.question_text: How can trip planning cut down on stressful driving situations?
sec03-card-sec03-F045.teaching_text: Building buffer minutes for congestion or storms removes the time pressure that triggers impatience and risky passing.

sec03-card-sec03-F046.question_text: What is the smart choice when strong emotions keep interfering with your ability to drive safely?
sec03-card-sec03-F046.teaching_text: Swapping seats when overwhelmed protects everyone far better than trying to tough out an emotional drive.

sec03-card-sec03-F047.question_text: How quickly does a parked car heat up during warm weather?
sec03-card-sec03-F047.teaching_text: Sunlight trapped through auto glass spikes cabin temperatures rapidly, turning even a quick errand stop deadly inside minutes.

sec03-card-sec03-F048.question_text: For how long is it acceptable to leave a child alone inside a vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F048.teaching_text: Even a two-minute dash into a store exposes an unattended child to heatstroke, power-window injury, or vehicle rollaway.

sec03-card-sec03-F049.question_text: What check should you perform every time before locking your vehicle and walking away?
sec03-card-sec03-F049.teaching_text: Scanning the whole interior with special focus on the back row catches sleeping infants before doors lock.

sec03-card-sec03-F050.question_text: What simple item-placement habit prompts you to check the back seat before leaving your car?
sec03-card-sec03-F050.teaching_text: Setting your bag, phone, or work badge on the rear floor forces you to open the back door at arrival.

sec03-card-sec03-F051.question_text: How should you store vehicle keys around kids, and what rule should children learn about parked cars?
sec03-card-sec03-F051.teaching_text: Children climbing into unlocked cars at home can get trapped in heat, so secure fobs high and forbid car play.

sec04-card-sec04-F001.question_text: What two vehicle-readiness habits apply before you start driving?
sec04-card-sec04-F001.teaching_text: Spotting a flat tire, fluid leak, or broken lamp in the driveway prevents dangerous roadside failures in traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F002.question_text: Which three tire conditions can create road-safety problems?
sec04-card-sec04-F002.teaching_text: Bald grooves hydroplane on wet asphalt while either overinflation or underinflation shrinks your tire's safe contact patch.

sec04-card-sec04-F003.question_text: How often does the New Hampshire manual recommend checking your tire pressure?
sec04-card-sec04-F003.teaching_text: Tires lose air gradually through seasonal temperature swings without looking visibly flat until handling and fuel economy suffer.

sec04-card-sec04-F004.question_text: Why must you set your seat and mirrors before moving the vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F004.teaching_text: Sliding seats or tilting mirrors while rolling pulls hands and eyes off traffic and risks improper airbag spacing.

sec04-card-sec04-F005.question_text: How should you sit in the driver's seat, and why is slouching risky?
sec04-card-sec04-F005.teaching_text: Slouching lets your hips submarine under the lap belt during a crash instead of holding your pelvis securely.

sec04-card-sec04-F006.question_text: Where should your heel rest as you move your foot between the accelerator and brake pedals?
sec04-card-sec04-F006.teaching_text: Anchoring your heel on the floorboard delivers smoother, faster pedal transitions than lifting your whole leg.

sec04-card-sec04-F007.question_text: How high should the steering wheel sit relative to your chin and shoulders?
sec04-card-sec04-F007.teaching_text: Aiming the wheel toward your chest rather than your face keeps sightlines open and supports safer airbag deployment.

sec04-card-sec04-F008.question_text: How many inches should separate your chest from the steering wheel, and what seat mistakes should you avoid?
sec04-card-sec04-F008.teaching_text: Sitting closer than ten inches puts you inside the airbag's inflation zone, while over-reclining ruins steering reach.

sec04-card-sec04-F009.question_text: Where should the head restraint sit behind your head to help prevent whiplash?
sec04-card-sec04-F009.teaching_text: A restraint dropped below ear height acts like a pivot in a rear-end hit instead of catching your head.

sec04-card-sec04-F010.question_text: How should you aim the interior rearview mirror and use its glare toggle?
sec04-card-sec04-F010.teaching_text: Framing the entire rear glass maximizes rearward awareness while flipping to night mode cuts blinding trailing headlights.

sec04-card-sec04-F011.question_text: Do properly adjusted mirrors eliminate every blind spot, or what habit must you add?
sec04-card-sec04-F011.teaching_text: Cars and motorcycles can hide beside your rear quarters outside mirror angles until a quick shoulder glance spots them.

sec04-card-sec04-F012.question_text: In what two ways do safety belts cut injury and fatality risk during a crash or swerve?
sec04-card-sec04-F012.teaching_text: Belts prevent deadly ejection and hold the driver behind the steering wheel during violent evasive maneuvers.

sec04-card-sec04-F013.question_text: For which age group does New Hampshire mandate safety restraints, and what does the manual recommend for everyone else?
sec04-card-sec04-F013.teaching_text: Exam takers must know New Hampshire's statutory mandate covers occupants under eighteen while strongly advising belts at every age.

sec04-card-sec04-F014.question_text: Where must the shoulder belt lie across your body, and which two placements are unsafe?
sec04-card-sec04-F014.teaching_text: Tucking a strap under your arm or behind your back concentrates crash force onto ribs or lets your torso slam forward.

sec04-card-sec04-F015.question_text: Where should the lap belt sit snugly, and what crash risk does that prevent?
sec04-card-sec04-F015.teaching_text: Anchoring low over strong hip bones stops occupants from sliding out underneath and prevents internal abdominal injuries.

sec04-card-sec04-F016.question_text: What commercial passenger-transport exception appears under New Hampshire's child-restraint rules?
sec04-card-sec04-F016.teaching_text: Taxis and similar vehicles that routinely transport paying passengers are carved out from the standard child-restraint mandate.

sec04-card-sec04-F017.question_text: Which two categories of school buses qualify under the child-restraint exception?
sec04-card-sec04-F017.teaching_text: Large buses topping ten thousand pounds use compartmentalized seating, and lighter buses originally built without belts are exempted too.

sec04-card-sec04-F018.question_text: Which vintage four-wheel and two-wheel vehicles are listed as child-restraint exceptions?
sec04-card-sec04-F018.teaching_text: Classic cars manufactured before factory seat belts existed and motorcycles both fall under the statutory exception list.

sec04-card-sec04-F019.question_text: When does an individual education plan create a restraint exception for a passenger under eighteen?
sec04-card-sec04-F019.teaching_text: When a student's documented individual education plan specifies that standard restraints pose a safety risk, an exception applies.

sec04-card-sec04-F020.question_text: Which age and height combination requires a child to ride in a federally approved child restraint?
sec04-card-sec04-F020.teaching_text: Notice the word both on exam questions because once a child reaches age seven or fifty-seven inches, booster rules shift.

sec04-card-sec04-F021.question_text: Do airbags replace safety belts, or how are the two systems designed to work?
sec04-card-sec04-F021.teaching_text: Airbags are engineered assuming occupants are belted, and riding unbuckled lets you slam into an inflating bag prematurely.

sec04-card-sec04-F022.question_text: How do seat belts assist airbag protection and help after the first impact?
sec04-card-sec04-F022.teaching_text: Airbags deflate instants after initial deployment, leaving your seat belt to protect you through rollovers or follow-up hits.

sec04-card-sec04-F023.question_text: Where should you look to learn exact details about the airbag system in your specific vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F023.teaching_text: Side-curtain layouts, passenger sensors, and child-seat switch rules vary by model and live inside your owner's manual.

sec04-card-sec04-F024.question_text: What is the legal status of driving with an unsecured load, and what if it causes a crash?
sec04-card-sec04-F024.teaching_text: Failing to tie down cargo endangers trailing traffic and exposes the driver to fines if loose items cause a wreck.

sec04-card-sec04-F025.question_text: What five cargo movements must a properly fastened load prevent on the road?
sec04-card-sec04-F025.teaching_text: Even sand sifting from a tailgate or lightweight trash blowing airborne counts as an improperly secured load.
sec04-card-sec04-F025.must_match_memory_hook: No sliding, shifting, dropping, sifting, flying

visual_sync.text_span: No sliding, shifting, dropping, sifting, flying

sec04-card-sec04-F026.question_text: What four requirements cover a towed trailer's wheels, bearings, guards, and tires?
sec04-card-sec04-F026.teaching_text: Dry wheel bearings seize at highway speed while missing fenders fling rocks and road spray into following windshields.

sec04-card-sec04-F027.question_text: Which six lamps and reflective items must a towed trailer carry?
sec04-card-sec04-F027.teaching_text: A trailer hides your tow vehicle's rear lights, requiring full tail, stop, turn, license-plate, side-marker, and reflector visibility.
sec04-card-sec04-F027.must_match_memory_hook: Tail, brake, turn, plate, side, reflectors

visual_sync.text_span: Tail, brake, turn, plate, side, reflectors

sec04-card-sec04-F028.question_text: How much accumulated snow and ice must you clear off your vehicle before driving on New Hampshire roads?
sec04-card-sec04-F028.teaching_text: Scraping just a windshield peephole violates New Hampshire's strict winter rule requiring roof, hood, and trunk clearing too.

sec04-card-sec04-F029.question_text: What two hazards do leftover snow and ice on a moving vehicle create?
sec04-card-sec04-F029.teaching_text: Roof snow slides forward over your windshield under braking or launches backward as heavy ice sheets into trailing windshields.

sec04-card-sec04-F030.question_text: How does the manual define conduct on New Hampshire roads that constitutes negligent driving?
sec04-card-sec04-F030.teaching_text: Driving with roof ice sheets, loose cargo, or careless maneuvers that endanger people or property triggers negligent-driving charges.

sec04-card-sec04-F031.question_text: What fine range applies to a first negligent-driving offense, and what happens on repeat offenses?
sec04-card-sec04-F031.teaching_text: Skipping five minutes with a snow brush can cost two hundred fifty to five hundred dollars first time and steeper penalties later.

sec05-card-sec05-F001.question_text: Which two clock positions are recommended on the steering wheel, and where do your thumbs and knuckles belong?
sec05-card-sec05-F001.teaching_text: Keeping thumbs and knuckles outside the rim stops a deploying airbag from snapping your hands backward.

sec05-card-sec05-F002.question_text: When should you use hand-to-hand steering versus hand-over-hand steering?
sec05-card-sec05-F002.teaching_text: Push-pull keeps your wrists clear of the steering hub on gentle curves while hand-over-hand handles tight parking corners.

sec05-card-sec05-F003.question_text: Without signs, signals, or a police officer directing traffic, which driver yields at an intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-F003.teaching_text: Checking right immediately at uncontrolled crossroads prevents side-impact crashes when two streets meet equally.

sec05-card-sec05-F004.question_text: To which oncoming vehicles must a driver turning left yield at an intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-F004.teaching_text: Misjudging an oncoming car's closing speed during a left turn is one of the top intersection crash causes.

sec05-card-sec05-F005.question_text: Why is knowing right-of-way law never an automatic green light to drive straight into an intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-F005.teaching_text: Legal rules assign who must yield, yet insisting on going when another driver blows a stop still wrecks your car.

sec05-card-sec05-F006.question_text: How must you respond when an emergency vehicle approaches with sirens or flashing lights from any direction?
sec05-card-sec05-F006.teaching_text: Stopping dead inside a crossroad traps ambulances and fire engines right where they need turning space.

sec05-card-sec05-F007.question_text: What two steps apply before pulling back onto the road after an emergency vehicle passes?
sec05-card-sec05-F007.teaching_text: A second patrol car or ambulance often trails the first, catching hasty drivers who pull out blind.

sec05-card-sec05-F008.question_text: Who goes first at an intersection, and how do you break a tie at a four-way stop?
sec05-card-sec05-F008.teaching_text: Clear arrival order and the right-hand tiebreaker prevent awkward hesitation waves at busy all-way stops.

sec05-card-sec05-F009.question_text: Who yields when pulling out of a driveway or private lane onto a public highway?
sec05-card-sec05-F009.teaching_text: Mainline drivers expect uninterrupted right-of-way past hidden residential aprons and private lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F010.question_text: Who yields when merging onto a limited-access highway or interstate?
