sec05-card-sec05-F010.teaching_text: Expecting fast freeway traffic to brake or swerve for your entrance ramp invites high-speed merge collisions.

sec05-card-sec05-F011.question_text: How must you treat pedestrians, cyclists, and vehicles that are already inside an intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-F011.teaching_text: Charging ahead the instant your side opens cuts off slower walkers and turning cars clearing the box.

sec05-card-sec05-F012.question_text: How do you recognize vehicles in a funeral procession behind a hearse, and what must you let them do?
sec05-card-sec05-F012.teaching_text: Cutting between cars running headlights behind a hearse splits an escorted group that expects to stay together.

sec05-card-sec05-F013.question_text: Which four live conditions must guide your speed so the vehicle stays under full control?
sec05-card-sec05-F013.teaching_text: Worn tires, heavy traffic, or thick fog can make even a moderate posted speed far too fast.

sec05-card-sec05-F014.question_text: What does a posted speed limit actually represent rather than a mandatory minimum pace?
sec05-card-sec05-F014.teaching_text: Treating a posted sign as a target during sleet or congestion confuses dry-day maximums with safe driving.

sec05-card-sec05-F015.question_text: What maximum speed does the New Hampshire manual state for a business or urban residential district?
sec05-card-sec05-F015.teaching_text: Dense crosswalks, curbside parked cars, and tight store driveways demand thirty-mile-per-hour stopping margins everywhere.

sec05-card-sec05-F016.question_text: Where does New Hampshire's thirty-five-mile-per-hour statutory speed limit apply?
sec05-card-sec05-F016.teaching_text: Spotting town homes outside compact urban cores cues thirty-five even before you pass another speed sign.

sec05-card-sec05-F017.question_text: Which two general speed limits cover other New Hampshire roadways outside special turnpike and I-93 zones?
sec05-card-sec05-F017.teaching_text: Knowing the forty-five and fifty-five baseline keeps rural state highway cruising legal between towns.

sec05-card-sec05-F018.question_text: Which interstates and multi-lane turnpikes fall under New Hampshire's sixty-five-mile-per-hour category?
sec05-card-sec05-F018.teaching_text: Central and eastern turnpikes only qualify for sixty-five where divided with at least four travel lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F019.question_text: What top speed applies on Interstate 93 from mile marker 45 north to the Vermont border?
sec05-card-sec05-F019.teaching_text: Test questions single out that exact northern I-93 stretch as New Hampshire's lone seventy-mile-per-hour corridor.

sec05-card-sec05-F020.question_text: What is the minimum speed on a New Hampshire interstate when road and weather conditions are good?
sec05-card-sec05-F020.teaching_text: Dropping below forty-five on clear dry freeway creates dangerous closing-speed gaps for traffic behind you.

sec05-card-sec05-F021.question_text: Why does driving far slower than normal traffic flow create a safety hazard?
sec05-card-sec05-F021.teaching_text: Frustrated drivers bottled up behind a creeping vehicle often gamble on tight lane swaps or passes.

sec05-card-sec05-F022.question_text: By how much and during what exact time windows must you lower speed in a posted school zone?
sec05-card-sec05-F022.teaching_text: Students arrive and dismiss inside those forty-five-minute windows before opening and after closing.

sec05-card-sec05-F023.question_text: How far ahead must you signal an ordinary turn versus a highway lane change or exit?
sec05-card-sec05-F023.teaching_text: Freeway speeds cover a hundred feet in barely a second, demanding five times the advance blinker distance.

sec05-card-sec05-F024.question_text: Why should you click your turn signal on even earlier during rain, snow, or fog?
sec05-card-sec05-F024.teaching_text: Drivers behind you need extra pavement to slow smoothly without skidding when traction drops.

sec05-card-sec05-F025.question_text: List the everyday maneuvers beyond corner turns that require your turn signal?
sec05-card-sec05-F025.teaching_text: Pulling from a curb, entering a driveway, merging, or pulling over all shift your path across others.

sec05-card-sec05-F026.question_text: How many front lamps must a passenger vehicle light, and between what sunset-to-sunrise times?
sec05-card-sec05-F026.teaching_text: A single working headlight mimics a motorcycle at night, hiding half your vehicle's width.

sec05-card-sec05-F027.question_text: During rain, snow, or fog, at what sight-distance threshold must your front headlamps go on?
sec05-card-sec05-F027.teaching_text: If people and cars blur inside a thousand feet, oncoming traffic needs your headlights to spot you.

sec05-card-sec05-F028.question_text: When is using your horn appropriate, and why should you skip unnecessary blasts?
sec05-card-sec05-F028.teaching_text: Startling cyclists or venting frustration with long blasts escalates road rage instead of preventing collisions.

sec05-card-sec05-F029.question_text: Near which two road users must you never sound your horn?
sec05-card-sec05-F029.teaching_text: Blind pedestrians rely on ambient traffic sound cues, and a spooked horse can bolt straight into lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F030.question_text: How much horn pressure is normally needed for an everyday safety warning?
sec05-card-sec05-F030.teaching_text: A brief tap catches attention cleanly without freezing or panicking the person you are warning.

sec05-card-sec05-F031.question_text: Name three situations where a light horn tap helps prevent a collision?
sec05-card-sec05-F031.teaching_text: Drivers reversing out of spots or drifting sideways often miss you in mirrors until a polite tap alerts them.

sec05-card-sec05-F032.question_text: From what mental moment to what final state is total stopping distance measured?
sec05-card-sec05-F032.teaching_text: Counting only brake-pad skid marks ignores the huge distance covered while your brain and foot react.

sec05-card-sec05-F033.question_text: How does raising your travel speed affect stopping time and stopping distance?
sec05-card-sec05-F033.teaching_text: Kinetic energy climbs faster than speed, compounding both reaction travel and physical braking rollout.

sec05-card-sec05-F034.question_text: What is perception time, and how long does it average for an alert driver?
sec05-card-sec05-F034.teaching_text: Even wide-awake eyes need nearly a second just to register brake lights or an obstacle ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F035.question_text: What physical movement defines reaction time, and what is its stated average span?
sec05-card-sec05-F035.teaching_text: Combined with perception time, nearly two full seconds pass at full speed before brake pads even touch.

sec05-card-sec05-F036.question_text: On dry pavement at fifty miles per hour with good brakes, roughly what stopping distance is needed?
sec05-card-sec05-F036.teaching_text: Half a football field on dry asphalt proves why close highway tailgating leaves zero physical survival margin.

sec05-card-sec05-F037.question_text: What minimum following-time cushion should you keep under normal New Hampshire driving conditions?
sec05-card-sec05-F037.teaching_text: Four seconds covers both perception and foot-reaction delays plus room to brake smoothly.

sec05-card-sec05-F038.question_text: What is the safest response when another driver follows you dangerously closely?
sec05-card-sec05-F038.teaching_text: Brake-checking or speeding up raises crash energy, whereas letting an aggressive tailgater ahead puts danger away from you.

sec05-card-sec05-F039.question_text: Walk through the visual checks and signal steps required before steering into a new lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F039.teaching_text: Taking one second look right after signaling catches fast cars that just slipped into your gap.

sec05-card-sec05-F040.question_text: How should you use a highway acceleration lane to join traffic smoothly?
sec05-card-sec05-F040.teaching_text: Matching existing traffic pace inside the merge lane prevents forcing mainline cars to slam their brakes.

sec05-card-sec05-F041.question_text: How should you set up for an upcoming highway exit?
sec05-card-sec05-F041.teaching_text: Positioning well ahead avoids dangerous last-second dives across multiple high-speed travel lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F042.question_text: Where do you hold highway speed and where do you slow down when taking a freeway exit?
sec05-card-sec05-F042.teaching_text: Waiting until your wheels enter the deceleration lane keeps fast mainline traffic flowing smoothly behind you.

sec05-card-sec05-F043.question_text: What two conditions must both be met before you start passing another vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F043.teaching_text: Broken yellow paint alone never makes a pass safe when glare, slick pavement, or heavy traffic interferes.

sec05-card-sec05-F044.question_text: Name the sightline and roadway locations where attempting to pass is strictly off-limits?
sec05-card-sec05-F044.teaching_text: Hidden oncoming traffic or side-entering cars turn blind crests, intersections, rail crossings, and narrow bridges into traps.

sec05-card-sec05-F045.question_text: Which lane serves passing on a multilane road, and when may you use a paved or unpaved shoulder to pass?
sec05-card-sec05-F045.teaching_text: Paved shoulders look wide enough to sneak around a turner yet hide stopped cars, cyclists, and gravel.

sec05-card-sec05-F046.question_text: What must you estimate before pulling out to overtake another vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F046.teaching_text: If oncoming or overtaken drivers must hit their brakes for you to squeeze back, the gap was too short.

sec05-card-sec05-F047.question_text: What three checks and signal move start a safe pass?
sec05-card-sec05-F047.teaching_text: Checking your left blind spot catches another car behind you that already pulled out to pass.

sec05-card-sec05-F048.question_text: What mirror visual tells you it is safe to signal and merge back after overtaking a vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F048.teaching_text: Seeing the whole front bumper in your interior mirror guarantees safe buffer space ahead of the passed car.

sec05-card-sec05-F049.question_text: How must you drive while another vehicle is overtaking you?
sec05-card-sec05-F049.teaching_text: Speeding up beside an overtaking car strands both vehicles alongside oncoming traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F050.question_text: What should you inspect before climbing into a parked vehicle to back up?
sec05-card-sec05-F050.teaching_text: Toddlers, pets, and low toys sit completely below trunk height where driver-seat sightlines miss them.

sec05-card-sec05-F051.question_text: Why are mirrors and over-the-shoulder head checks alone not enough to clear every inch behind your car?
sec05-card-sec05-F051.teaching_text: Rear bodywork blocks a wedge of pavement right behind the bumper regardless of how far you twist.

sec05-card-sec05-F052.question_text: How fast should you reverse, and which way do you turn the steering wheel when backing?
sec05-card-sec05-F052.teaching_text: Turning the top of the wheel right swings the rear bumper right, and slow throttle prevents oversteering.

sec05-card-sec05-F053.question_text: Where must you look while backing through a turn, and how long do you keep looking back?
sec05-card-sec05-F053.teaching_text: Your front fenders swing wide during reverse turns while primary danger stays behind until wheels stop.

sec05-card-sec05-F054.question_text: How should you use a rear backup camera alongside mirrors and head checks?
sec05-card-sec05-F054.teaching_text: Narrow camera lenses miss cross-traffic cars and pedestrians approaching rapidly from the sides.

sec05-card-sec05-F055.question_text: When must you slow down for a curve, and what three factors call for slowing even more?
sec05-card-sec05-F055.teaching_text: Poor grip, close followers, or a hidden curve exit leave zero margin if you carry straightaway speed inward.

sec05-card-sec05-F056.question_text: What happens to your tires if you brake hard after already entering a curve?
sec05-card-sec05-F056.teaching_text: Tires already working sideways to hold the corner overload and slide straight when spiked with heavy braking.

sec05-card-sec05-F057.question_text: Why must you reduce speed at the very first sign of rain, snow, sleet, or ice?
sec05-card-sec05-F057.teaching_text: Early moisture mixes with road film immediately, stretching braking rollout and loosening cornering bite.

sec05-card-sec05-F058.question_text: What happens between your steering tires and the pavement during hydroplaning?
sec05-card-sec05-F058.teaching_text: Once water lifts front rubber off the road surface, turning the wheel stops steering the car.

sec05-card-sec05-F059.question_text: Which speed habit and two tire checks lower your risk of hydroplaning?
sec05-card-sec05-F059.teaching_text: Healthy tread channels and proper PSI push standing water aside instead of letting a wedge build underneath.

sec05-card-sec05-F060.question_text: What route decision should you make when facing a flooded road or deep standing water?
sec05-card-sec05-F060.teaching_text: Hidden washouts and stalling depths turn driving through pooled floodwater into an avoidable trap.

sec05-card-sec05-F061.question_text: What three adjustments belong on unpaved gravel or dirt roads?
sec05-card-sec05-F061.teaching_text: Loose stones roll like marbles beneath braking tires, lengthening stops and kicking dust or chips behind.

sec05-card-sec05-F062.question_text: How should you position your car and watch ahead on a narrow rural road?
sec05-card-sec05-F062.teaching_text: Wide trucks or oncoming cars cutting tight rural bends often drift across unpainted center space.

sec05-card-sec05-F063.question_text: How do drivers share a single-lane rural bridge?
sec05-card-sec05-F063.teaching_text: Heeding narrow-bridge signs and yielding to whoever reaches the span first prevents head-on standoffs.

sec05-card-sec05-F064.question_text: Why do steel bridges or open deck gratings call for lower speed, extra following gap, and a firm grip?
sec05-card-sec05-F064.teaching_text: Slick steel ribs tug slightly at tire grooves and lengthen braking, especially when damp.

sec05-card-sec05-F065.question_text: How must you drive where roadside brush, hill crests, or blind corners block your view?
sec05-card-sec05-F065.teaching_text: Hidden driveways, walkers, or farm trucks can sit just past overgrown foliage or a sharp crest.

sec05-card-sec05-F066.question_text: How should you approach an uncontrolled rural intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-F066.teaching_text: Without stop signs or lights, cross-road drivers can enter fast from behind trees or cornfields.

sec05-card-sec05-F067.question_text: What fundamental visibility limit makes night driving more hazardous than daytime travel?
sec05-card-sec05-F067.teaching_text: Darkness shrinks your preview window down to whatever short cone your headlamp beams illuminate.

sec05-card-sec05-F068.question_text: When may you run high-beam headlights at night, and when must you switch to low beams?
sec05-card-sec05-F068.teaching_text: Dimming for oncoming cars and when trailing ahead prevents blinding other drivers directly or via mirrors.

sec05-card-sec05-F069.question_text: Why must you select low beams instead of high beams in fog, rain, or snow?
sec05-card-sec05-F069.teaching_text: Airborne droplets and snowflakes reflect high beams straight back into your eyes like a bright wall.

sec05-card-sec05-F070.question_text: Where should you aim your eyes if bright oncoming headlights dazzle you at night?
sec05-card-sec05-F070.teaching_text: Guiding off the right edge line keeps you centered safely without bleaching out your night vision.

sec05-card-sec05-F071.question_text: What visual clues should you scan ahead and along both edges of the road at night?
sec05-card-sec05-F071.teaching_text: Unlit pedestrians, cyclists, and deer show up first as dark outlines or eye reflections near shoulders.

sec05-card-sec05-F072.question_text: Why should you skip tinted or colored eyewear at night or on overcast days?
sec05-card-sec05-F072.teaching_text: Any dark or colored tint filters precious contrast when ambient light is already scarce.

sec05-card-sec05-F073.question_text: By how many extra seconds should you lengthen your following gap at night, and on unfamiliar dark roads?
sec05-card-sec05-F073.teaching_text: Stacking one or two extra seconds onto the four-second baseline offsets reduced night depth perception.

sec05-card-sec05-F074.question_text: How do vehicle warning technologies communicate hazards, and what do they NOT do automatically?
sec05-card-sec05-F074.teaching_text: Assuming a chime or flashing icon will steer or stop the car for you leads straight into collisions.

sec05-card-sec05-F075.question_text: How should a safe driver treat modern driver-assistance alerts relative to mirrors and head checks?
sec05-card-sec05-F075.teaching_text: Sensors get blocked by slush, dirt, or sharp angles, so active human scanning stays mandatory.

sec05-card-sec05-F076.question_text: Which four visual sources should you monitor together whenever backing a vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F076.teaching_text: Rotating across all three mirrors, direct shoulder views, and the screen catches cross traffic from every angle.

sec05-card-sec05-F077.question_text: When does a reversing camera switch on, and what does it show?
sec05-card-sec05-F077.teaching_text: Instant rear-bumper video helps spot low curbs or toys right behind the trunk lid.

sec05-card-sec05-F078.question_text: How does a backup warning system notify you when an obstruction sits behind your car in reverse?
sec05-card-sec05-F078.teaching_text: Audible tones or seat vibrations alert you even while your eyes sweep side mirrors during backing.

sec05-card-sec05-F079.question_text: Even when your car has a blind-spot monitor, what two checks must you still perform before changing lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F079.teaching_text: Fast-closing motorcycles or cars two lanes over can slip past sensor zones without a direct head check.

sec05-card-sec05-F080.question_text: What specific mistake triggers a vehicle's curve-speed warning system?
sec05-card-sec05-F080.teaching_text: Early speed alerts prompt you to shed momentum on the straightaway before lateral cornering forces build.

sec05-card-sec05-F081.question_text: What camera views and optional sensor alerts does a surround-view monitor combine?
sec05-card-sec05-F081.teaching_text: Stitching a top-down perimeter image with sonar chimes helps clear tight poles and curbs at low speed.

sec05-card-sec05-F082.question_text: What does forward-collision warning scan for ahead, and what action does that warning alone NOT take?
sec05-card-sec05-F082.teaching_text: Warning-only systems chime for slower or stopped cars ahead while counting on your foot to press the brake.

sec06-card-sec06-F001.question_text: What active habits and avoided behaviors form the foundation of safe driving in traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-F001.teaching_text: Combining sign literacy and speed compliance with avoiding fatigue, tailgating, impairment, and distraction stops wrecks early.

sec06-card-sec06-F002.question_text: What wins when a police officer's hand signal conflicts with a posted sign or traffic light?
sec06-card-sec06-F002.teaching_text: Live officers manage crashes, power outages, or detours that static lights cannot see.

sec06-card-sec06-F003.question_text: Which three physical road features and three authorized people count as official traffic-control devices?
sec06-card-sec06-F003.teaching_text: Highway flaggers and school crossing guards carry official traffic-control authority right alongside signals and police.

sec06-card-sec06-F004.question_text: What must you check and yield to before proceeding on a steady green traffic light?
sec06-card-sec06-F004.teaching_text: Green permits cautious entry only after leftover pedestrians and turning cars clear the crossroad.

sec06-card-sec06-F005.question_text: What exact transition does a steady yellow traffic light warn you is about to happen?
sec06-card-sec06-F005.teaching_text: Flooring the gas on yellow gambles against cross traffic right as the red phase begins.

sec06-card-sec06-F006.question_text: Where must your vehicle come to a stop when facing a steady red traffic signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F006.teaching_text: Creeping past the painted stop bar pushes your front bumper directly into pedestrian walking space.

sec06-card-sec06-F007.question_text: Under what two conditions may you turn right during a steady red signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F007.teaching_text: Rolling through red without halting or missing a no-turn-on-red sign triggers automatic citations and crosswalk danger.

sec06-card-sec06-F008.question_text: How should you drive through an intersection displaying a flashing yellow signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F008.teaching_text: Flashing yellow flags busy side-street hazards without requiring a dead stop unless cross traffic enters.

sec06-card-sec06-F009.question_text: What stop and right-of-way steps are required at a flashing red traffic signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F009.teaching_text: Treat a flashing red bulb identically to a stop sign before pulling into crossing lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F010.question_text: What movement does a lighted green arrow allow, and what duty still applies first?
sec06-card-sec06-F010.teaching_text: Even a protected arrow requires letting straggling pedestrians or clearing cars finish crossing safely.

sec06-card-sec06-F011.question_text: When is the only time you may move while facing a steady red arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-F011.teaching_text: Unlike a circular red ball, a steady red arrow locks that movement unless another active lamp permits going.

sec06-card-sec06-F012.question_text: May a pedestrian step into the street while facing a steady red arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-F012.teaching_text: Stepping off the curb against a red arrow puts walkers across live protected turning lanes unless a walk head lights.

sec06-card-sec06-F013.question_text: Which four visual design elements let road signs communicate rules, warnings, directions, and services?
sec06-card-sec06-F013.teaching_text: Distinct outlines and background colors tell you a sign's message from afar even when snow or glare blurs text.

sec06-card-sec06-F014.question_text: Contrast the meaning of red road-sign coloring with green road-sign coloring?
sec06-card-sec06-F014.teaching_text: Red demands immediate stops or bans, whereas green overhead boards point toward exits and destinations.

sec06-card-sec06-F015.question_text: What does a blue highway sign indicate compared with a yellow highway sign?
sec06-card-sec06-F015.teaching_text: Spotting yellow ahead cues caution for curves or merges, while blue marks rest stops, gas, or hospitals.

sec06-card-sec06-F016.question_text: What message category belongs to white signs versus orange signs?
sec06-card-sec06-F016.teaching_text: White boards enforce speed and lane laws every day, while bright orange warns of temporary construction hazards.

sec06-card-sec06-F017.question_text: Match brown, pink, and purple highway sign backgrounds to what each color identifies?
sec06-card-sec06-F017.teaching_text: New Hampshire tests pink emergency incident signs and purple electronic toll tags alongside classic brown park signs.

sec06-card-sec06-F018.question_text: Which sign has eight sides, and which sign uses a downward-pointing triangle?
sec06-card-sec06-F018.teaching_text: Unique silhouettes let you recognize a stop or yield obligation even from the back side at an unfamiliar crossroad.

sec06-card-sec06-F019.question_text: What does a pennant-shaped sign warn about, and on which side of the road is it posted?
sec06-card-sec06-F019.teaching_text: Posting the yellow pennant on the left edge keeps it visible even when a tall truck ahead blocks right-side posts.

sec06-card-sec06-F020.question_text: What category of road message appears on a diamond-shaped sign?
sec06-card-sec06-F020.teaching_text: Whether bearing words or a symbol, every diamond alerts you to an upcoming physical or traffic hazard.

sec06-card-sec06-F021.question_text: What do rectangular signs communicate compared with five-sided pentagon signs?
sec06-card-sec06-F021.teaching_text: Recognizing the house-like five-sided silhouette cues immediate vigilance for children near school crossings.

sec06-card-sec06-F022.question_text: How does a circular railroad sign differ in placement and role from a railroad crossbuck?
sec06-card-sec06-F022.teaching_text: Early circular signs give braking space down the road, whereas the white X crossbuck stands right at the rails.

sec06-card-sec06-F023.question_text: In what order of pavement features must your wheels come completely stationary at a stop sign?
sec06-card-sec06-F023.teaching_text: Knowing the fallback order stops you from blocking unmarked pedestrian paths when paint has faded.

sec06-card-sec06-F024.question_text: Once your wheels stop at a stop sign, what must you do before pulling out?
sec06-card-sec06-F024.teaching_text: Stopping legally is only half the rule if you pull forward without checking for walkers and cross traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F025.question_text: What speed and right-of-way actions are required when approaching a yield sign?
sec06-card-sec06-F025.teaching_text: Be ready to halt completely whenever priority vehicles or pedestrians occupy the path ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-F026.question_text: What road conditions do warning signs flag, and what driver response might they require?
sec06-card-sec06-F026.teaching_text: Spotting a warning early lets you shed speed smoothly instead of panic-braking at a hidden curve.

sec06-card-sec06-F027.question_text: What panel shapes and five rule topics belong to standard regulatory signs?
sec06-card-sec06-F027.teaching_text: Direction, lane use, turn bans, speed ceilings, and parking rules carry legal ticket authority.

sec06-card-sec06-F028.question_text: What does a red circle with a red diagonal slash across a symbol mean?
sec06-card-sec06-F028.teaching_text: Universal slash symbols communicate bans like no U-turn or no left turn across every language instantly.

sec06-card-sec06-F029.question_text: Which four tiers of highway networks are distinguished by route-marker shapes and colors?
sec06-card-sec06-F029.teaching_text: Telling an interstate shield apart from a U.S. or New Hampshire state marker keeps navigation on track.

sec06-card-sec06-F030.question_text: Which compass directions correspond to even-numbered versus odd-numbered interstate highways?
sec06-card-sec06-F030.teaching_text: Checking parity on I-89, I-93, or I-95 confirms north-south travel versus east-west routes instantly.

sec06-card-sec06-F031.question_text: According to the New Hampshire handbook, how does a three-digit route starting with an odd digit differ from an even one?
sec06-card-sec06-F031.teaching_text: For example, I-293 loops around Manchester while an odd-prefix route branches into an urban area.

sec06-card-sec06-F032.question_text: What shapes and three background colors are used on guide signs for directions, places, and services?
sec06-card-sec06-F032.teaching_text: Grouping highway exits in green, parks in brown, and traveler services in blue speeds up freeway decisions.

sec06-card-sec06-F033.question_text: What actions should you take when you spot a circular advance railroad warning sign?
sec06-card-sec06-F033.teaching_text: Not every rural crossing has gates or bells, so active looking and listening starts at the advance circle.

sec06-card-sec06-F034.question_text: When a train approaches a railroad crossing, where or how many feet back must you stop?
sec06-card-sec06-F034.teaching_text: Stopping closer than fifteen feet exposes your front end to wide locomotive overhang and lowering gates.

sec06-card-sec06-F035.question_text: At a railroad crossing with more than one set of tracks, when is it safe to pull across?
sec06-card-sec06-F035.teaching_text: The caboose of one passing train frequently hides a second fast train approaching on the adjacent track.

sec06-card-sec06-F036.question_text: Once a railroad crossing is clear in both directions, how must you drive across the tracks?
sec06-card-sec06-F036.teaching_text: Entering tracks when traffic ahead could trap your rear bumper on the rails invites catastrophic train strikes.

sec06-card-sec06-F037.question_text: Which two categories of commercial vehicles must stop at every railroad crossing even when no train is coming?
sec06-card-sec06-F037.teaching_text: Mass casualties or explosive cargo leave zero margin for missed signals at rail intersections.

sec06-card-sec06-F038.question_text: What should you anticipate whenever following a school bus, transit bus, or hazmat tanker toward railroad tracks?
sec06-card-sec06-F038.teaching_text: Drivers staring past the bus at open gates get caught off guard when its brake lights flare before the rails.

sec06-card-sec06-F039.question_text: What condition qualifies the maximum legal speed printed on a speed-limit sign?
sec06-card-sec06-F039.teaching_text: Darkness, glare, or winter slush require dropping below the printed number on the white rectangle.

sec06-card-sec06-F040.question_text: Which single maneuver may use a shared center lane, and which two uses are banned?
sec06-card-sec06-F040.teaching_text: Cruising straight or passing down a two-way turn lane sets up head-on collisions with opposing left turners.

sec06-card-sec06-F041.question_text: What rule governs travel wherever a one-way sign is posted?
sec06-card-sec06-F041.teaching_text: Turning against a one-way arrow puts you head-on across every lane of oncoming city traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F042.question_text: What text color, background color, and two panel shapes mark standard highway work-zone signs?
sec06-card-sec06-F042.teaching_text: High-visibility orange diamonds and rectangles stand out immediately against trees, asphalt, and permanent yellow warnings.

sec06-card-sec06-F043.question_text: Name the crew, traffic, and pavement hazards commonly announced by orange work-zone warnings?
sec06-card-sec06-F043.teaching_text: Milled pavement lips and slow dump trucks entering lanes demand lower speed and wide cushions.

sec06-card-sec06-F044.question_text: What legal weight do a work-zone flagger's paddle or hand signals carry?
sec06-card-sec06-F044.teaching_text: Flaggers coordinate single-lane alternating traffic around blind construction bends where green lights cannot.

sec06-card-sec06-F045.question_text: What two jobs do orange cones, barrels, panels, and temporary barriers perform in a work zone?
sec06-card-sec06-F045.teaching_text: Cutting between cones enters open trenches, wet concrete, or active worker footpaths.

sec06-card-sec06-F046.question_text: How should you adjust when approaching temporary signals inside a construction zone?
sec06-card-sec06-F046.teaching_text: Portable red lights often sit before narrow one-lane bridges where stopped queues build out of sight.

sec06-card-sec06-F047.question_text: Where do drivers learn that traffic fines are doubled for a work zone?
sec06-card-sec06-F047.teaching_text: Advance penalty signs remove any excuse once you cross into the active construction corridor.

sec06-card-sec06-F048.question_text: Which four traffic-organization tasks do painted road markings handle?
sec06-card-sec06-F048.teaching_text: Reading paint lines alongside upright signs tells you lane direction, passing legality, and exact stop bars.

sec06-card-sec06-F049.question_text: How does traffic flow differ across a broken white line compared with a broken yellow line?
sec06-card-sec06-F049.teaching_text: Yellow on your left always warns that crossing the stripe puts you nose-to-nose with oncoming traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F050.question_text: Does a broken lane line guarantee you can pull out and pass at any moment?
sec06-card-sec06-F050.teaching_text: Dashed paint lifts the legal ban, leaving you responsible for checking oncoming cars and clear sightlines.

sec06-card-sec06-F051.question_text: May you pass or switch lanes across a solid white stripe in New Hampshire?
sec06-card-sec06-F051.teaching_text: Solid white channel lines protect turn pockets, tunnels, and tight merges from abrupt lane weaving.

sec06-card-sec06-F052.question_text: Where a solid yellow line runs beside a broken yellow line, which stripe governs your passing right?
sec06-card-sec06-F052.teaching_text: Solid on your side forbids passing while dashed on your side allows passing when oncoming space is clear.

sec06-card-sec06-F053.question_text: Where do white road-edge lines appear versus yellow road-edge lines?
sec06-card-sec06-F053.teaching_text: Seeing yellow along your left curb or median confirms a one-way roadway or divided highway.

sec06-card-sec06-F054.question_text: Walk through the three-step stopping-place order at intersections with or without painted lines?
sec06-card-sec06-F054.teaching_text: Stopping behind the first applicable boundary keeps crosswalks and cross-street sightlines open.

sec06-card-sec06-F055.question_text: After halting at the legal stopping line, what must happen before you pull forward?
sec06-card-sec06-F055.teaching_text: Edging out cautiously after checking left and right catches cross traffic hidden earlier by buildings or trees.

sec06-card-sec06-F056.question_text: Must you yield to pedestrians crossing at an intersection that has no painted crosswalk lines?
sec06-card-sec06-F056.teaching_text: Every street corner forms a legal crosswalk extension whether white stripes are painted on the asphalt or not.

sec06-card-sec06-F057.question_text: What do large white arrows painted inside approach lanes tell drivers at intersections?
sec06-card-sec06-F057.teaching_text: Going straight out of a mandatory turn-arrow pocket sideswipes drivers turning legally beside you.

sec06-card-sec06-F058.question_text: Who uses a shared middle turning lane, and what two misuses are prohibited?
sec06-card-sec06-F058.teaching_text: Entering only shortly before your left turn keeps the shared middle pocket clear for both directions.

sec09-card-sec09-F001.question_text: How does the New Hampshire manual define defensive driving?
sec09-card-sec09-F001.teaching_text: Scanning ahead for unlawful moves or lapses around you lets you adjust speed or lane position before metal meets.

sec09-card-sec09-F002.question_text: Does obeying every traffic rule yourself mean you can stop watching for mistakes around you?
sec09-card-sec09-F002.teaching_text: Having legal right-of-way never prevents a collision when a distracted motorist, pedestrian, or cyclist steps out unexpectedly.

sec09-card-sec09-F003.question_text: What should you do right after a collision if your vehicle can still be moved?
sec09-card-sec09-F003.teaching_text: Pulling a drivable car off live lanes keeps traffic flowing past the scene and prevents pileups behind you.

sec09-card-sec09-F004.question_text: What number should you call right away when a collision causes injuries?
sec09-card-sec09-F004.teaching_text: Dialing nine-one-one dispatches paramedics and law enforcement together so trauma care starts as quickly as possible.

sec09-card-sec09-F005.question_text: How should you assist injured crash victims, and when may an injured person be moved?
sec09-card-sec09-F005.teaching_text: Arranging an ambulance while keeping hurt occupants still prevents worsening spinal trauma unless immediate danger forces movement.

sec09-card-sec09-F006.question_text: Why must everyone in a collision swap names and mailing addresses on scene?
sec09-card-sec09-F006.teaching_text: Accurate names and mailing addresses ensure insurers, courts, and involved parties can reach everyone after leaving the scene.

sec09-card-sec09-F007.question_text: Which two pieces of driver-license information should you write down from every involved motorist?
sec09-card-sec09-F007.teaching_text: Writing down a license number without the state that issued it makes out-of-state verification slow and incomplete.

sec09-card-sec09-F008.question_text: Which plate and vehicle-identification details should you gather for every car in the crash?
sec09-card-sec09-F008.teaching_text: Matching plate numbers and issuing states against each vehicle's make, model, and year prevents mix-ups on claim forms.

sec09-card-sec09-F009.question_text: Beyond driver and car specs, what coverage and bystander details belong in your crash notes?
sec09-card-sec09-F009.teaching_text: Independent witnesses leave scenes quickly, so recording their names and addresses alongside insurance and injured contacts protects accuracy.

sec09-card-sec09-F010.question_text: Which crashes require filing a DMV report within fifteen days when not covered by a police investigation?
sec09-card-sec09-F010.teaching_text: Even modest bumper repairs cross one thousand dollars combined quickly, triggering the fifteen-day DMV filing clock.

sec09-card-sec09-F011.question_text: Do you have to file a separate DMV crash report when a police officer investigates and files one?
sec09-card-sec09-F011.teaching_text: An investigating officer's report fulfills the mandatory DMV filing, leaving your own operator report optional rather than required.

sec09-card-sec09-F012.question_text: From which three places can you get a New Hampshire Operator Accident Report form?
sec09-card-sec09-F012.teaching_text: Whether you prefer downloading online or picking up paper locally, DMV counters, agency forms pages, and police stations stock it.

sec09-card-sec09-F013.question_text: Who may submit the crash report if injuries prevent the driver from completing it?
sec09-card-sec09-F013.teaching_text: Hospitalized drivers do not miss the reporting window when a rider from the trip or the registered owner files instead.

sec09-card-sec09-F014.question_text: What does the manual advise if you are unsure whether combined crash damage tops one thousand dollars?
sec09-card-sec09-F014.teaching_text: Hidden structural or sensor repairs routinely blow past initial curbside guesses, so filing protects your legal compliance.

sec09-card-sec09-F015.question_text: Does New Hampshire require all drivers to buy auto insurance upfront, and what happens after an uninsured crash?
sec09-card-sec09-F015.teaching_text: Exam takers often confuse no mandatory upfront purchase with zero accountability, when an uninsured wreck triggers strict financial-responsibility rules.

sec09-card-sec09-F016.question_text: Which costs can an uninsured driver be held personally responsible for after causing a collision?
sec09-card-sec09-F016.teaching_text: Driving without liability coverage leaves your personal savings and wages exposed to the other party's repair and hospital bills.

sec09-card-sec09-F017.question_text: What must the DMV do if an uninsured driver cannot pay property and medical claims from a crash?
sec09-card-sec09-F017.teaching_text: Unpaid uninsured crash claims lock out your driving privileges automatically until you reach an accepted settlement.

sec09-card-sec09-F018.question_text: How may an uninsured driver have to prove insurance for several years after a collision?
sec09-card-sec09-F018.teaching_text: Once an uninsured crash hits your record, keeping privileges requires your insurance carrier to maintain an SR-twenty-two certificate.

sec09-card-sec09-F019.question_text: How does an impaired-driving conviction affect both license and vehicle-registration restoration?
sec09-card-sec09-F019.teaching_text: Impaired-driving convictions block both your driver license and plate registration from returning until SR-twenty-two proof is filed.

sec09-card-sec09-F020.question_text: What crash-scene offense appears on the conviction list requiring insurance proof before reinstatement?
sec09-card-sec09-F020.teaching_text: Leaving an involved collision without stopping and reporting triggers mandatory financial-responsibility filings before reinstatement.

sec09-card-sec09-F021.question_text: Does a motor-vehicle homicide conviction trigger mandatory insurance proof before reinstatement?
sec09-card-sec09-F021.teaching_text: Any homicide conviction arising from operating a motor vehicle requires verified insurance filings before privileges can ever return.

sec09-card-sec09-F022.question_text: At which reckless-driving conviction count does proof of insurance become required to restore privileges?
sec09-card-sec09-F022.teaching_text: Watch the offense count on test questions because a second reckless-driving conviction triggers the mandatory insurance-proof rule.

sec09-card-sec09-F023.question_text: Besides specific listed convictions, what administrative review of your violation record can require insurance proof?
sec09-card-sec09-F023.teaching_text: Even without a single headline crime, a troubling pattern of traffic tickets reviewed at a just-cause hearing can mandate coverage.
